a146.speaker: The Africa Report (report)
a146.name: The Africa Report (report)
a146.speech: “In dozens of viral TikTok edits, Traore leads imaginary armies, topples Western empires and is hailed as the ‘new Thomas Sankara.’ The captions, bold and uncompromising, include ‘Africa’s Messiah!’ ‘The People’s Captain!’ and ‘France Must Fall.’”

a146.speaker: The Africa Report (report)
a146.name: The Africa Report (report)
a146.speech: “His rhetoric still falls short of real, measurable improvements in security and civic freedoms. There’s a gap between his message and the reality on the ground, something that will ultimately test his legitimacy and legacy.”

a146.speaker: Ibrahim Traore, Burkinabe leader
a146.name: Ibrahim Traore
a146.title: Burkinabe leader
a146.speech: By his word, when he overthrew the government of President Paul-Henri Sandaogo Damiba in September 2022 and announced himself as head of the new Patriotic Movement for Safeguard and Restoration (PMSR), he promised to hand over power back to civilians in two years — that was in 2024; he hasn’t said a word about any possible new date yet. He rallied support by giving speeches against Western imperialism and colonialism, vowing to create conditions at home to stem youth migration and tackle insurgency.

a146.speaker: Emmanuel Macron, President of France
a146.name: Emmanuel Macron
a146.title: President of France
a146.speech: Described the relationship between France and Francophone West Africa as “part of a civilising obligation.”

a146.speaker: Tom Burgis, author of The Looting Machine (book)
a146.name: Tom Burgis
a146.title: author of The Looting Machine (book)
a146.speech: Writes that in Niger the French state-owned atomic energy group Areva’s profit from uranium is twice Niger’s GDP.

a146.speaker: Ernest Harsch, author of Burkina Faso: A History of Power, Protest and Revolution (book)
a146.name: Ernest Harsch
a146.title: author of Burkina Faso: A History of Power, Protest and Revolution (book)
a146.speech: Said of Sankara: “In a conscious effort at nation-building, the revolutionary government also promoted a new national identity…that revolutionary project succeeded in altering the contours of the state and social and political life.”

a146.speaker: Azu Ishiekwene, Editor-in-Chief of LEADERSHIP (author of the article)
a146.name: Azu Ishiekwene
a146.title: Editor-in-Chief of LEADERSHIP (author of the article)
a146.speech: Argues that Traore is not Sankara but an opportunist and impostor, and that what Traore needs now is not clout-chasing or AI propaganda by Russian-backed Wagner, but sober-minded commitment to turn around the fortunes of his country, one step at a time.

a192.speaker: World Bank, Africa's Pulse report (32nd edition, "Pathways to Job Creation in Africa")
a192.name: World Bank
a192.title: Africa's Pulse report (32nd edition, "Pathways to Job Creation in Africa")
a192.speech: Projects Sub-Saharan Africa's growth to reach 3.8 percent in 2025, up from 3.5 percent in 2024, attributing the slight acceleration to easing inflationary pressures and a modest recovery in investment, despite persistent global economic uncertainties.

a192.speaker: World Bank, Africa's Pulse report
a192.name: World Bank
a192.title: Africa's Pulse report
a192.speech: Warns that downside risks remain substantial, including the indirect effects of global trade policy uncertainty, declining investor appetite, and a shrinking pool of external finance, including reduced official development assistance.

a192.speaker: World Bank
a192.name: World Bank
a192.speech: Says countries must focus on accelerating growth that generates high-quality jobs; the report outlines policy priorities including reducing the cost of doing business, investments in infrastructure, human capital and skills development, and strengthening institutions and governance, and identifies agribusiness, mining, tourism, healthcare, housing and construction as key sectors with potential to drive job creation.

a192.speaker: Andrew Dabalen, World Bank Chief Economist for the Africa Region
a192.name: Andrew Dabalen
a192.title: World Bank Chief Economist for the Africa Region
a192.speech: “Over the next quarter century, Sub-Saharan Africa’s working-age population will grow by more than 600 million” ; “The challenge will be matching this growing population with better jobs, given that only 24 percent of new workers today land wage-paying jobs. A structural shift toward more medium and large firms is essential to generate wage jobs at scale.”

a322.speaker: Hassan Sheikh Mohamud, President of the Federal Republic of Somalia
a322.name: Hassan Sheikh Mohamud
a322.title: President of the Federal Republic of Somalia
a322.speech: Commended Ambassador Waern for his efforts in strengthening the longstanding relationship between the two nations during his tenure, and acknowledged Sweden's consistent support for Somalia in areas including development cooperation, peacebuilding, governance and humanitarian assistance.

a322.speaker: Joachim Waern, outgoing Swedish Ambassador to Somalia
a322.name: Joachim Waern
a322.title: outgoing Swedish Ambassador to Somalia
a322.speech: Expressed gratitude to the Somali government and people for the cooperation and hospitality extended to him throughout his mission, and reaffirmed Sweden's continued support for Somalia's development journey and the shared commitment to democratic values and mutual respect.

a332.speaker: Konou Idohou Léontine, president of the NGO RIFONGA-Benin
a332.name: Konou Idohou Léontine
a332.title: president of the NGO RIFONGA-Benin
a332.speech: Said it is important to have enough women in decision-making bodies at all levels, and specifically at the level of Benin’s municipalities in March 2013, because for her the project comes at just the right time to remedy a social injustice.

a332.speaker: Michaël Raynor, United States Ambassador to Benin
a332.name: Michaël Raynor
a332.title: United States Ambassador to Benin
a332.speech: Deplored the weak representation of women at the various levels of Benin’s socio-political life, basing himself on the numbers of women in the National Assembly and among communal councillors; said the stakes of this eighteen-month project are high, and expressed the wish that the record number of women in major political bodies in the United States at the last presidential contests would set an example for Benin.

a332.speaker: Raphaël Edou, Minister of Decentralisation, Local Authorities and Regional Planning
a332.name: Raphaël Edou
a332.title: Minister of Decentralisation, Local Authorities and Regional Planning
a332.speech: Spoke of the opportunities to be seized in this project before proceeding with its official launch; while recognising women’s predisposition to management and the importance of the initiative, he urged the women present to take the necessary steps because, according to him, the task will not be an easy one.

a543.speaker: Souleymane Ouedraogo, national director of Educo Benin
a543.name: Souleymane Ouedraogo
a543.title: national director of Educo Benin
a543.speech: "During this year 2019, a budget of approximately 787,200,000 CFA francs will be invested from our own funds in the development of projects and programmes in Benin. With 19 local partner NGOs working in co-construction, 4 programmes will be implemented in Borgou, Alibori, Atlantique, Oueme and Littoral."

a543.speaker: Educo Benin (organisation statement)
a543.name: Educo Benin (organisation statement)
a543.speech: As an organisation centred on children's rights, welcomes UNESCO's initiative in proclaiming the International Day of Education, sharing the conviction that while education is an end in itself, it is also the best way to guarantee rights, well-being and the dignity of life; notes that 75 million children and young people of school age worldwide need educational support, largely because education is traditionally the least funded area of humanitarian aid, with less than 3% of total global funding; and reiterates its commitment to work alongside sister organisations, local partners, State technical services, communes, communities and children themselves for lasting social change: "Together, we must ensure that children learn every day and are not left behind."

a597.speaker: Tewolde Yohannes, manager of Orotta National Referral Hospital
a597.name: Tewolde Yohannes
a597.title: manager of Orotta National Referral Hospital
a597.speech: Stated that from 22 September to 5 October, cardiac surgeries were conducted on 79 children in collaboration with German medical experts, and that earlier in the year, from 6 to 19 February, surgeries were performed on 24 children in partnership with Italian medical specialists.

a597.speaker: Alem Demoz and Silvio Liyoni, coordinators of the 'Med-Action Bambini' program
a597.name: Alem Demoz and Silvio Liyoni
a597.title: coordinators of the 'Med-Action Bambini' program
a597.speech: Noted that surgeries on six children were successfully performed by Eritrean medics; they added that efforts are underway to enable Eritrean medical experts to independently perform these surgeries in the future.

a597.speaker: Kahsai Seium, head of the eye treatment unit at Keren Hospital
a597.name: Kahsai Seium
a597.title: head of the eye treatment unit at Keren Hospital
a597.speech: Reported that screenings were conducted across all administrative areas of the sub-zone to identify patients requiring surgery.

a597.speaker: The medical experts who performed the surgeries
a597.name: The medical experts who performed the surgeries
a597.speech: Commended the public's growing awareness, as evidenced by the increasing number of people visiting health facilities for eye treatment.

a719.speaker: Recep Tayyip Erdogan, Turkish President
a719.name: Recep Tayyip Erdogan
a719.title: Turkish President
a719.speech: As Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan has repeatedly underlined in every platform for many months, Israel’s aggression must be stopped for regional peace and global stability to be achieved.

a719.speaker: Recep Tayyip Erdogan, Turkish President
a719.name: Recep Tayyip Erdogan
a719.title: Turkish President
a719.speech: As Erdogan repeatedly asserts: “The world is bigger than five” and “a fairer world is possible.”

a782.speaker: WHO study on priority endemic pathogens
a782.name: WHO study on priority endemic pathogens
a782.speech: The first global effort to systematically prioritize endemic pathogens based on their regional and global health impact; it reconfirms longstanding priorities for vaccine research and development, including for HIV, malaria, and tuberculosis - three diseases that collectively cause nearly 2.5 million deaths each year - and gives attention to pathogens such as Group A streptococcus, which contributes to 280,000 deaths from rheumatic heart disease, and Klebsiella pneumoniae, a bacteria associated with 790,000 deaths in 2019 and responsible for 40 per cent of neonatal deaths due to sepsis in low-income countries.

a782.speaker: Dr. Mateusz Hasso-Agopsowicz, WHO vaccine research
a782.name: Dr. Mateusz Hasso-Agopsowicz
a782.title: WHO vaccine research
a782.speech: Said the study aims to shift the focus in vaccine development away from commercial returns towards regional and global health needs, explaining that in the past vaccine R&D typically was influenced by profitability so that diseases severely affecting low-income regions received little attention: "We hope this represents a critical shift where we want to change the focus from commercial perspective profitability of new vaccines towards the actual health burden so that the new vaccine research and development is driven by health burden and not just commercial opportunities." ; "We had asked experts that have expertise in pathogen epidemiology, clinicians, paediatricians, vaccine experts from all of the WHO regions, so that to ensure that the list and the results that we produce, they really reflect the needs of diverse populations worldwide." ; said the study is expected to guide future vaccine R&D investments, including by funders, researchers and vaccine developers, but also policymakers as they "can decide whether to introduce these vaccines into immunization programmes."

a1025.speaker: World Bank
a1025.name: World Bank
a1025.speech: According to the World Bank, over 70% of Malawians live on less than $2.15 per day.

a1205.speaker: UN investigators (new OHCHR report)
a1205.name: UN investigators (new OHCHR report)
a1205.speech: In a new report, UN investigators detailed multiple attacks on civilians, healthcare facilities, markets, and schools, as well as ethnically motivated summary executions. Among its key recommendations, the report called for expanding the arms embargo and the jurisdiction of the International Criminal Court (ICC) to cover the whole of Sudan – not just the region of Darfur.

a1205.speaker: Volker Türk, UN High Commissioner for Human Rights
a1205.name: Volker Türk
a1205.title: UN High Commissioner for Human Rights
a1205.speech: "The continued and deliberate attacks on civilians and civilian objects, as well as summary executions, sexual violence and other violations and abuses, underscore the utter failure by both parties to respect the rules and principles of international humanitarian and human rights law" ; "Some of these acts may amount to war crimes. They must be investigated promptly and independently, with a view to bringing those responsible to justice," he added.

a1205.speaker: OHCHR report (UN human rights report)
a1205.name: OHCHR report (UN human rights report)
a1205.speech: The report highlighted the widespread use of sexual violence as a weapon of war, with 120 documented incidents affecting at least 203 victims. Cases are likely vastly underreported due to fear, stigma, and the collapse of medical and judicial institutions. All sides involved in the fighting have been responsible for violations, according to report, including widespread sexual violence. The report also detailed widespread disappearances and a generalised crackdown on civic space, including killings of journalists and attacks on human rights defenders. At least 12 journalists were killed, two of them while in detention, and 31 were arbitrarily detained, including four women. In all, throughout 2024, OHCHR documented more than 4,200 civilian killings in the context of hostilities though the real number is likely much higher.

a1205.speaker: Volker Türk, UN High Commissioner for Human Rights
a1205.name: Volker Türk
a1205.title: UN High Commissioner for Human Rights
a1205.speech: "The persistent use of sexual violence as a weapon of war in Sudan is deeply shocking" ; "Urgent steps must be taken by the parties to put an end to it, to hold those responsible to account and provide redress for survivors," he stressed.

a1205.speaker: Li Fung, head of the OHCHR office in Sudan
a1205.name: Li Fung
a1205.title: head of the OHCHR office in Sudan
a1205.speech: described the dire situation in Sudan as a "dangerous tipping point". Speaking to journalists at the UN Office at Geneva (UNOG) via video link from Port Sudan, she underscored the need for the international community to renew the focus on human rights. "[The international community] must take all necessary measures to protect civilians and prevent further violations and abuses. It remains urgent to ensure critical humanitarian assistance can reach those in need," she said. "Together, we must stand with the people of Sudan."

a1213.speaker: US State Department (report distributed by APO Group on its behalf)
a1213.name: US State Department (report distributed by APO Group on its behalf)
a1213.speech: According to the report, the delegation will travel to northern Ghana to launch the Coastal States Stability Mechanism (CSSM), jointly developed by USAID and Germany, and will discuss CSSM initiatives aimed at expanding and improving government delivery of essential services and supporting efforts to promote social and economic resilience in the face of instability and conflict. They will meet local government officials, traditional leaders and civil society representatives to discuss further collaboration on strengthening security, preventing conflict and promoting long-term stability in northern Ghana.

a1464.speaker: Ulisses Correia e Silva, Prime Minister of Cape Verde
a1464.name: Ulisses Correia e Silva
a1464.title: Prime Minister of Cape Verde
a1464.speech: Said in parliament, during the opening of the debate "The present and future of the Cape Verdean economy: strategies for sustainable growth and innovation": "Cape Verde today depends less on foreign aid and the future trend is towards ever less aid. This reality demands increasingly incisive, innovative and sustainable policies to promote economic growth driven by private sector investment and by exports, in an environment of macroeconomic stability." ; According to the Prime Minister, this internal consolidation allows the State to pay the salaries of civil servants, magistrates, doctors, nurses and teachers and to guarantee the functioning of the justice, health, security and education sectors with ever less recourse to foreign aid.

a1464.speaker: Ulisses Correia e Silva, Prime Minister of Cape Verde
a1464.name: Ulisses Correia e Silva
a1464.title: Prime Minister of Cape Verde
a1464.speech: Considers that this change is due, in large part, to the economic recovery recorded after the COVID-19 pandemic, with growth of 7.3% in 2024, controlled inflation of 1%, and a consistent reduction in public debt, unemployment and poverty: "The economy is growing robustly and the results directly touch people. We have less unemployment, which went from 15% in 2016 to 8%, less poverty, which fell from 35.5% in 2015 to 24.7% in 2023, and more young people employed. Youth unemployment went from 41% in 2016 to 20.1% currently."

a1464.speaker: Ulisses Correia e Silva, Prime Minister of Cape Verde
a1464.name: Ulisses Correia e Silva
a1464.title: Prime Minister of Cape Verde
a1464.speech: Said that in this new cycle the government is betting strongly on integrated policies that stimulate private investment, innovation, exports and economic diversification, and pointed to tourism, the blue economy, the digital economy and the energy transition as strategic pillars for the sustainability of growth: "We are creating the conditions for the economy to become more resilient to external shocks. We want growth that is sustainable, that increases household income and that contributes to territorial cohesion and economic empowerment."

a1464.speaker: Ulisses Correia e Silva, Prime Minister of Cape Verde
a1464.name: Ulisses Correia e Silva
a1464.title: Prime Minister of Cape Verde
a1464.speech: Announced the intention to gradually reduce the Corporate Income Tax to 15% by 2030 and to review the Personal Income Tax, benefiting above all the lowest incomes and the middle class ; "Soon, we will launch the Morabeza Fund, with the support of the AfDB, worth 24 million dollars, to promote entrepreneurship and innovation in the digital economy. We will continue to invest in young people, with more qualifications, more financing and more opportunities."

a1930.speaker: Mohamud Ahmed Adan (Geesood), Minister of Commerce and Industry of the Federal Government of Somalia
a1930.name: Mohamud Ahmed Adan (Geesood)
a1930.title: Minister of Commerce and Industry of the Federal Government of Somalia
a1930.speech: Highlighted the critical importance of fostering an effective and results-oriented economic partnership. He stated that such a collaboration is essential for accelerating the development of Somalia's domestic trade and industrial sectors, which are key pillars of the national economic agenda.

a1930.speaker: Minister Mohamud Ahmed Adan (Geesood) and Alper Aktas, Ambassador of the Republic of Turkiye to Somalia
a1930.name: Minister Mohamud Ahmed Adan (Geesood) and Alper Aktas
a1930.title: Ambassador of the Republic of Turkiye to Somalia
a1930.speech: Reaffirmed their commitment to strengthening the working relationship and advancing the shared trade and investment goals of Somalia and Turkiye, concluding with a strong mutual agreement from both sides to further intensify their cooperation.

a2073.speaker: Hassan Sheikh Mohamud, President of the Federal Republic of Somalia
a2073.name: Hassan Sheikh Mohamud
a2073.title: President of the Federal Republic of Somalia
a2073.speech: At the 6th round of the United Nations conference on climate change in Nairobi, Kenya, he called for more action and support to mitigate the effects of climate change on vulnerable countries like Somalia.

a2126.speaker: USAID (statement/directive posted on the USAID website)
a2126.name: USAID (statement/directive posted on the USAID website)
a2126.speech: "all USAID direct hire personnel will be placed on administrative leave globally, with the exception of designated personnel responsible for mission-critical functions, core leadership and specially designated programs" ; The statement said it is preparing a plan for personnel posted outside the United States "under which the Agency would arrange and pay for return travel to the United States within 30 days" and terminate "contracts that are not determined to be essential." ; The statement on the website ends with: "Thank you for your service."

a2139.speaker: Mrs. Schessler, Ukrainian human rights activist living in Russia (interviewee)
a2139.name: Mrs. Schessler
a2139.title: Ukrainian human rights activist living in Russia (interviewee)
a2139.speech: Said she left Ukraine in May 2014, that she was coordinator of the anti-Maidan movement in the city of Nikolaev and that criminal proceedings were opened against her: "We were demanding federal status for the regions of south-eastern Ukraine. But no one wanted at that time to separate the south-east from Ukraine. A great many comrades were imprisoned. I was able to escape that by leaving Ukraine." ; Said the criminal proceedings brought against her in Ukraine are continuing and have only been temporarily suspended, and that the ban on speaking Russian, which began in 2014, is linked to the fact that Ukraine is not a federal state and that the regions do not have the right to speak their regional language and to support their regional culture and values.

a2139.speaker: Mrs. Schessler, Ukrainian human rights activist living in Russia (interviewee)
a2139.name: Mrs. Schessler
a2139.title: Ukrainian human rights activist living in Russia (interviewee)
a2139.speech: Said the opposition in Ukraine is being physically destroyed and that many politically active people have disappeared without a trace or been imprisoned, such as Elena Berezhnaya, a well-known human rights activist who defended the rights of political prisoners and spoke before the UN Human Rights Committee, the OSCE and the European Parliament: "She has been in prison since March 2022 and no one knows what state of health she is in. No one can visit her, not even members of her family." ; Named the historian Aleksander Karewin, arrested in March 2022 for working on the shared history of Russia and Ukraine, and the energy expert Dmitri Marunich, in prison since April 2022 for giving interviews to various media including Russian ones, saying "no one knows under which article of the criminal code they want to charge him." ; Said a former colleague from the Nikolaev city council, over 70, was accused of supporting Russian movements for leading the "Immortal Regiment", and that two women residents of Snigerovka were arrested and accused of pro-Russian activities for distributing humanitarian aid and helping people apply for Russian pensions, facing ten-year prison sentences: "What I am telling you is only the tip of the iceberg."

a2139.speaker: Mrs. Schessler, Ukrainian human rights activist living in Russia (interviewee)
a2139.name: Mrs. Schessler
a2139.title: Ukrainian human rights activist living in Russia (interviewee)
a2139.speech: Said lawyers are obstructed: "Elena Berezhnaya has a lawyer, but he does not communicate anything to the public. Everyone is afraid to disclose the slightest information." ; Said the Kyiv lawyer Valentin Rybin had to leave Ukraine in March 2022 because his work gave rise to criminal investigations, that many lawyers have been forced to leave Ukraine, and that the well-known Kharkov lawyer Dmitri Tikhonenkov was arrested in March 2022 and later released on bail: "Ukrainian lawyers are unable to pass information to Western countries because they are intimidated and imprisoned. Today it takes a great deal of courage to protect political prisoners in Ukraine, and in fact such protection is no longer possible."

a2139.speaker: Mrs. Schessler, Ukrainian human rights activist living in Russia (interviewee)
a2139.name: Mrs. Schessler
a2139.title: Ukrainian human rights activist living in Russia (interviewee)
a2139.speech: Said that lists of political prisoners exist but many relatives are afraid to add their arrested loved ones' details, fearing serious consequences, and hope they will be exchanged or released against large bail payments of several hundred thousand euros. ; Cited the Russian Orthodox activist Dmitri Skvarzov and the former head of the Union of "Left Forces" Vassili Volga as having been released against very large bail payments, and the journalist Yuri Tkachev, editor-in-chief of the Odessa website "Timer", arrested in March 2022 and released under house arrest after reportedly paying two million hryvnias, about 50,000 euros: "He has been silenced like many, many others."

a2139.speaker: Mrs. Schessler, Ukrainian human rights activist living in Russia (interviewee)
a2139.name: Mrs. Schessler
a2139.title: Ukrainian human rights activist living in Russia (interviewee)
a2139.speech: Said that in the parts of the Kherson and Kharkov regions from which the Russian army has withdrawn "there is today total terror", that people have been arrested and accused of supporting the Russian armed forces although they were only distributing humanitarian aid, and that teachers who prepared lists for participation in the referendum are being prosecuted: "They are arrested and then disappear, and for many of them we do not know where they are. There are no lawyers and no way to search for these missing people. People are in great danger today."

a2139.speaker: Mrs. Schessler, Ukrainian human rights activist living in Russia (interviewee)
a2139.name: Mrs. Schessler
a2139.title: Ukrainian human rights activist living in Russia (interviewee)
a2139.speech: Said the Ukrainian secret service SBU searched several Russian Orthodox monasteries, including the Trinity-Sergius Lavra in Kyiv, claiming to look for Russian underground fighters: "The SBU invents things to justify the political persecution of religious dignitaries." ; Said the Ukrainian Orthodox Church of the Russian Patriarchate has been persecuted for several years by the authorities in Kyiv because it brings together Ukrainians and Russians, and that "shared faith is a crime from the point of view of the Kyiv authorities."

a2139.speaker: Mrs. Schessler, Ukrainian human rights activist living in Russia (interviewee)
a2139.name: Mrs. Schessler
a2139.title: Ukrainian human rights activist living in Russia (interviewee)
a2139.speech: Said that in Ukraine anyone can be stopped in the street and asked to show their phone and the Telegram channels they subscribe to, and that anyone subscribed to a well-known Russian channel such as colonelcassad or Juri Podoljaka can be arrested and questioned: "When my friends in Ukraine leave home, they delete all their Telegram channels. Many YouTube channels and many websites are blocked in Ukraine. They can only be viewed via a VPN."

a2139.speaker: Mrs. Schessler, Ukrainian human rights activist living in Russia (interviewee)
a2139.name: Mrs. Schessler
a2139.title: Ukrainian human rights activist living in Russia (interviewee)
a2139.speech: Listed the best-known political assassinations of recent years in Ukraine: the alleged suicide in March 2015 of the former governor of the Zaporozhye region Aleksandr Peklushenko, which she said was in reality a political assassination; the shooting of Party of Regions member Oleg Kalashnikov on 15 April 2015; the shooting of journalist and writer Oles Buzina on 16 April 2015; and the death of Valentina Semenyuk, chairwoman of the State Property Privatization Fund, in August 2014, presented as a suicide. "The essential point is that it is known who committed these murders. However no one has been held responsible... the result of these murders is that they have spread fear."

a2139.speaker: Mrs. Schessler, Ukrainian human rights activist living in Russia (interviewee)
a2139.name: Mrs. Schessler
a2139.title: Ukrainian human rights activist living in Russia (interviewee)
a2139.speech: Gave her forecast for Ukraine's future: "Ukraine as a sovereign state has already ceased to exist. The territory is under the total control of the Americans and is used as a means of fighting against Russia."

a2292.speaker: United States Agency for International Development (USAID)
a2292.name: United States Agency for International Development (USAID)
a2292.speech: has unveiled a funding opportunity aimed at bolstering child protection initiatives in Ghana; through its newly released Notice of Funding Opportunity (NOFO), USAID invites applications from eligible entities to implement the "Child Protection Activity" program.

a2292.speaker: USAID Notice of Funding Opportunity (Reference Number: 72064125RFA00001)
a2292.name: USAID Notice of Funding Opportunity (Reference Number: 72064125RFA00001)
a2292.speech: seeks innovative and impactful proposals that align with USAID's mission of sustainable development and safeguarding vulnerable children; the program, open to both local and international organizations, emphasizes collaboration with Ghanaian development partners to address child protection challenges effectively.

a2318.speaker: Federal High Court judge (court order)
a2318.name: Federal High Court judge (court order)
a2318.speech: ordered the arrest and summons of Temesgen Yilma, one of the seven individuals and three companies charged for alleged money laundering, usury and engaging in illegal remittance services; the Court ordered his arrest as the defendant failed to appear before the Court after receiving a warrant.

a2318.speaker: Federal prosecutors’ charge (court record)
a2318.name: Federal prosecutors’ charge (court record)
a2318.speech: The charge accuses Azeb Mehreteab of entering into a 50-million-Br loan deal with Haileyesus Mengistu, with Haregewoin Tedla signing the loan agreement on Azeb’s behalf and Efrem Mulatu signing as a witness for the loan that had nine percent of usurious interest rates for six months ; While agreeing to lend Haileyesus the money, Azeb took the title deed of his seven-storey building, estimated to be worth 250 million Br, as collateral, then transferred 3.2 million Br of the loan into Haileyesus’ account, and prepared a document showing JJ Properties bought the building for 60 million Br; however, Haileyesus did not sign the agreement, reads the charge ; After realising Haileyesus did not sign the agreement, the defendants charged him for allegedly taking 19.8 million Br, according to the prosecutors, and also pressured him to negotiate for the transfer of his entire shares at Cosmo Trading, his ownership of the seven-storey building, an excavator, three vehicles, and construction machinery into their ownership.

a2318.speaker: Federal prosecutors’ charge (court record)
a2318.name: Federal prosecutors’ charge (court record)
a2318.speech: The charge accuses Azeb and Temesgen of taking over the managerial positions at Cosmo Trading and receiving 71 million Br in bank loans as working capital and using 21 million Br of this amount to service Cosmo’s debt; the charge also claims that they allegedly transferred 32 million Br in two rounds into JJ Properties’ account ; An additional seven million Birr was transferred into Boston Real Estate’s account, while 16 million Br was also used to recover TTH Trading’s debt, claims the charge; the prosecutors also charged Temesgen for allegedly taking 14.4 million Br in rental fees earned from the building and 1.4 million Br from a grader’s sale ; Temesgen and Haregewoin, with two more defendants, are charged under the third count for allegedly engaging in illegal remittance services, transferring local money into recipients’ local account while the foreign currency transactions were taking place in the United States and Europe, leading the government to lose over 383,000 dollars, claims the charge ; According to the charge, Temesgen took 49 million Br from the accounts of Cosmo and Haileyesus and transferred it to his siblings’ and companies’ accounts, and Azeb transferred 9.9 million Br into the accounts of different individuals; the charge accused them of concealing the illegally obtained money by passing it through banking transfers.

a2318.speaker: Judge Yenenesh Bahiru, Federal High Court
a2318.name: Judge Yenenesh Bahiru
a2318.title: Federal High Court
a2318.speech: adjourned the case for March 5, 2021, to receive the Immigration Nationality & Vital Events Agency report about the three defendants who are abroad; the Judge also ordered police to dispatch a warrant to the remaining defendants and to arrest and bring Temesgen to the next session.

a2318.speaker: Federal High Court (court orders)
a2318.name: Federal High Court (court orders)
a2318.speech: In June, while the case was under investigation, the Court issued a restraining order on the properties administered by the defendants; two months later, following a request from the public prosecutor, the Court issued another order for forming a neutral third-party body that will administer the properties that are under court injunction.

a2441.speaker: Filippo Grandi, United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees
a2441.name: Filippo Grandi
a2441.title: United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees
a2441.speech: Issued a solemn appeal for international solidarity on World Refugee Day, hailing “the courage and resilience of millions of people forced to flee war, violence and persecution,” while underlining the growing seriousness of the threats they face ; “Persistent conflicts – from Sudan to Ukraine, from the DRC to Gaza – are causing untold suffering. And those who flee are too often unjustly stigmatised.”

a2441.speaker: Filippo Grandi, United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees
a2441.name: Filippo Grandi
a2441.title: United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees
a2441.speech: Warned of the massive reduction in humanitarian aid, which jeopardises the survival of millions of displaced people.

a2441.speaker: Filippo Grandi, United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees
a2441.name: Filippo Grandi
a2441.title: United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees
a2441.speech: Pointed, from Damascus, to a rare sign of hope, the return of two million Syrians to their country after the fall of Bashar Al-Assad's regime: “Today I met families who are returning to their homes after more than a decade. Their deep emotion illustrates the strength of the bond with one's native land.”

a2441.speaker: Filippo Grandi, United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees
a2441.name: Filippo Grandi
a2441.title: United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees
a2441.speech: Paid tribute to the host countries and communities which, often in difficult conditions, continue to open their doors to refugees, and called on the wealthiest states, financial institutions and companies to assume their share of responsibility: “Support for these generous hosts is essential to keep the flame of solidarity alive.”

a2441.speaker: Filippo Grandi, United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees
a2441.name: Filippo Grandi
a2441.title: United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees
a2441.speech: Concluded: “Even in a world beset by instability, moments of reconstruction and hope are possible” ; “If we act together, refugees, strong in their courage and ingenuity, will actively take part in building a fairer and more humane future.”

a2441.speaker: Latest UNHCR data
a2441.name: Latest UNHCR data
a2441.speech: More than 122 million people worldwide have been forcibly displaced, a record figure.

a2543.speaker: Stakeholders at the 13th Annual International Conference of the Population Association of Nigeria (PAN)
a2543.name: Stakeholders at the 13th Annual International Conference of the Population Association of Nigeria (PAN)
a2543.speech: Warned that the country's reproductive health system is at a crossroads following the recent withdrawal of USAID's funding for Family Planning (FP) services in Nigeria ; The experts noted that Nigeria had relied heavily on donor support to sustain its FP programmes for many years. According to them, this has ensured millions of women have access to contraceptives and reproductive health services. However, that support is rapidly disappearing, leaving the country at a critical crossroads ; The experts also called for increased funding for FP initiatives to address Nigeria's demographic challenges and improve reproductive health outcomes ; Experts warn that without proper funding, FP programmes may collapse, leading to more unintended pregnancies and maternal deaths.

a2543.speaker: Ejike Oji, Chairperson of the Association for the Advancement of Family Planning (AAFP)
a2543.name: Ejike Oji
a2543.title: Chairperson of the Association for the Advancement of Family Planning (AAFP)
a2543.speech: Recounted how he recently received a letter confirming the worst fears of many in the sector. "The letter, dated 20 January, informed me that USAID would be halting its funding for a key family planning programme, pending a 90-day review," Mr Oji said. According to him, this move follows a growing trend of international donors pulling out, citing Nigeria's failure to deliver measurable progress despite years of investment ; "We were in a meeting years ago when a USAID official bluntly asked us, 'Why should we keep funding you when we are not seeing results?' Now, they have finally decided to walk away," he said ; He said that without donor support, contraceptive supplies would dwindle, leading to a surge in unintended pregnancies, unsafe abortions, and increased maternal deaths. He noted that Nigeria's reproductive health system, already fragile, could collapse under the strain, undoing years of progress.

a2543.speaker: USAID official (anonymous, quoted by Ejike Oji)
a2543.name: USAID official (anonymous
a2543.title: quoted by Ejike Oji)
a2543.speech: "Why should we keep funding you when we are not seeing results?"

a2543.speaker: Ejike Oji, Chairperson of the Association for the Advancement of Family Planning (AAFP)
a2543.name: Ejike Oji
a2543.title: Chairperson of the Association for the Advancement of Family Planning (AAFP)
a2543.speech: Said the national budget for family planning was reduced by 90 per cent in 2019 due to insufficient counterpart funding to match donor grants. This cut resulted in stock-outs of contraceptive commodities at Primary Health Centres, further limiting women's access to essential family planning services. He said the trend of underfunding continued, with the 2024 budget allocating only N2.2 billion to FP programmes, representing 0.16 per cent of the overall health budget.

a2543.speaker: Fatima Mairami, obstetrician and gynaecologist
a2543.name: Fatima Mairami
a2543.title: obstetrician and gynaecologist
a2543.speech: Emphasised the need to prioritise family planning as a critical public health issue. Ms Mairami described family planning as a sustainable solution to the challenges posed by the country's rapid population growth.

a2543.speaker: Ijeoma Nwankwo, Senior Programme Officer for the Pharmaceutical Society of Nigeria Foundation (PSNF)
a2543.name: Ijeoma Nwankwo
a2543.title: Senior Programme Officer for the Pharmaceutical Society of Nigeria Foundation (PSNF)
a2543.speech: Said the reduction in funding has increased pressure on the private sector to fill the gap, straining their capacity to provide adequate services ; Ms Nwankwo noted that the funding cut has also denied many individuals access to contraceptives, limiting availability for both married and unmarried women, thereby exacerbating the challenges of FP services in the country.

a2543.speaker: Ijeoma Nwankwo, Senior Programme Officer for the Pharmaceutical Society of Nigeria Foundation (PSNF)
a2543.name: Ijeoma Nwankwo
a2543.title: Senior Programme Officer for the Pharmaceutical Society of Nigeria Foundation (PSNF)
a2543.speech: She highlighted the role of technology in addressing the gaps created by funding cuts in family planning initiatives. She noted that leveraging technology can help increase access to contraceptives and family planning services, especially for underserved populations. According to her, digital platforms can be utilised to provide education on family planning options, connect individuals with healthcare providers, and facilitate the delivery of contraceptives. "Technology offers a scalable and innovative approach to bridging the gaps caused by funding cuts. By using digital tools, we can ensure that FP services reach those who need them the most, even in the most remote areas," she explained.

a2553.speaker: National Agency for the Control of AIDS (NACA)
a2553.name: National Agency for the Control of AIDS (NACA)
a2553.speech: Says information on social media regarding the withdrawal of subsidy for Antiretroviral therapy (ART) is false.

a2553.speaker: Temitope Ilori, Director-General of the National Agency for the Control of AIDS (NACA)
a2553.name: Temitope Ilori
a2553.title: Director-General of the National Agency for the Control of AIDS (NACA)
a2553.speech: Said in a statement that the claim that ART will now cost N250,000 per dose, with patients required to pay N500,000 monthly, is false and misleading: “We want to categorically state that HIV treatment in Nigeria remains free of charge at government-approved health facilities” ; “We give thanks to donor agencies, including the US President's Emergency Plan for AIDS Relief (PEPFAR), the Global Fund, and other development partners for their continued support” ; “There has been no withdrawal of funding or support from the US Government, USAID, or the World Health Organisation (WHO) regarding HIV treatment in Nigeria” ; reaffirmed the agency's commitment to ensuring uninterrupted access to HIV treatment and said collaboration with donor partners remained steadfast.

a2553.speaker: Temitope Ilori, Director-General of the National Agency for the Control of AIDS (NACA)
a2553.name: Temitope Ilori
a2553.title: Director-General of the National Agency for the Control of AIDS (NACA)
a2553.speech: Urged the public to disregard the misinformation and avoid unnecessary panic, adding that NACA's priority is to sustain the progress made in controlling HIV/AIDS in Nigeria, and cautioned against the spread of unverified information, as it can cause unnecessary fear and hinder efforts to combat HIV/AIDS: “We encourage Nigerians to rely on verified sources for health-related information. NACA remains committed to ensuring that no person living with HIV is denied access to life-saving treatment due to misinformation or fear” ; encouraged the public to visit the agency's official website or follow its verified social media platforms for accurate and up-to-date information on HIV treatment and prevention.

a2563.speaker: Dangote Refinery management / Dangote organisation (press release, November 3, 2024)
a2563.name: Dangote Refinery management / Dangote organisation (press release
a2563.title: November 3, 2024)
a2563.speech: Alleged that: “…An international trading company has recently hired a depot facility next to the Dangote Refinery, with the objective of using it to blend substandard products that will be dumped into the market to compete with Dangote Refinery’s higher quality products.”

a2563.speaker: Pinnacle Oil & Gas (statement)
a2563.name: Pinnacle Oil & Gas (statement)
a2563.speech: Noted that as the only depot close to the Dangote Refinery in the area, it was responding to clear the air on the matter raised by the refinery; contended that as a company with a history of integrity and with strict compliance with the existing regulations, it cannot distribute products that are low quality to Nigerians ; “Pinnacle Oil & Gas has the only depot facility next to the Dangote Refinery. Without equivocation, we state that Pinnacle Oil & Gas would never engage or attempt to import or distribute any off-spec or substandard product into the Nigerian market. Our company has a reputation for integrity and regulatory compliance which is extremely important to us.”

a2563.speaker: Pinnacle Oil & Gas (statement)
a2563.name: Pinnacle Oil & Gas (statement)
a2563.speech: Contended that in a deregulated environment, the system works a lot better when it is allowed to have multiple buyers and multiple sellers; argued that it was the right thing for Nigerians to have supply options whether for imported fuels or locally refined ones, and that when this is allowed to happen, the lowest sustainable price will then be established ; “Deregulated commodity markets work best with an open system of multiple sellers and multiple buyers bidding to establish the market price. For Nigeria to have supply options that include local refineries or imports is the mechanism that will establish the lowest sustainable prices. A free market is also regulated to ensure that all products meet the country’s specifications and that all players behave responsibly.”

a2616.speaker: Hilaria Mukapuli, Swapo member of parliament
a2616.name: Hilaria Mukapuli
a2616.title: Swapo member of parliament
a2616.speech: Submitted the report of the standing committee on natural resources, which contains recommendations on aquaculture projects that fall under the fisheries ministry, following a visit in May to the ministry of fisheries’ aquaculture projects in the Kavango East and West, Omusati, Oshana, Omaheke and //Karas regions: “In fulfilling its objectives, the committee visited and had meetings with regional governors, regional councils and ministry of fisheries staff in the regions and meetings with communities (cooperatives) managing fish farms in addition to site visits of all fish farms and research centres.”

a2616.speaker: Hilaria Mukapuli, Swapo member of parliament
a2616.name: Hilaria Mukapuli
a2616.title: Swapo member of parliament
a2616.speech: Noted that there is potential to “exploit the demand and produce fish for local consumption and export” ; said “the introduction of aquaculture farming remains a noble idea capable of exponential growth to feed the nation, albeit the substantial investment required to achieve the objectives. Despite the challenges, fish farms continue to operate, providing much-needed protein to locals at affordable rates.”

a2616.speaker: Hilaria Mukapuli, Swapo member of parliament
a2616.name: Hilaria Mukapuli
a2616.title: Swapo member of parliament
a2616.speech: Highlighting challenges the committee observed, said “fish production is seasonal due to the lack of greenhouse plastic covers and roofs required to produce fish all year, thus limiting fish farms to produce at maximum capacity”; explained that plastic roofing is not durable enough to withstand strong winds – especially in the south: “As a result, they are constantly being blown off and breaking up at fish farms where they are in place”; said the committee realised that poor quality feed sourced from Zambia has an impact on production capacity, and “budget constraints to repair broken equipment and ponds” are limiting fish farms from attaining full production levels; “Fish meal availability is limited and expensive, as the companies involved mainly produce it for export markets.”

a2618.speaker: Siafa Jallah, deputy director of press relations at the Liberian Senate
a2618.name: Siafa Jallah
a2618.title: deputy director of press relations at the Liberian Senate
a2618.speech: Confirmed that Prince Yomie Johnson died on Thursday at a local hospital in Paynesville, a suburb of the capital city, Monrovia.

a2618.speaker: Truth and Reconciliation Commission (TRC) report
a2618.name: Truth and Reconciliation Commission (TRC) report
a2618.speech: Identified Prince Yomie Johnson as one of the “most notorious perpetrators” of heinous acts; the Commission’s investigations revealed numerous grave accusations against him, including involvement in killings, extortion of civilians, orchestrating massacres, and engaging in acts of both torture and rape; the TRC named him as a principal figure responsible for egregious acts during the conflict and specifically called for his prosecution for war crimes, crimes against humanity, and various severe violations of international humanitarian law.

a2618.speaker: Joseph Boakai, President of Liberia (executive order)
a2618.name: Joseph Boakai
a2618.title: President of Liberia (executive order)
a2618.speech: Took a significant step towards addressing the grievances of civil war victims by signing an executive order to establish a long-awaited war and economic crimes court, intended to provide a platform for justice and accountability for those affected by the atrocities committed during the civil wars.

a2697.speaker: Dr. Louise Mapleh Kpoto, Liberia's Minister of Health
a2697.name: Dr. Louise Mapleh Kpoto
a2697.title: Liberia's Minister of Health
a2697.speech: Praised the collective efforts of Liberia's partners: "We are deeply grateful to our donor and implementing partners for their continuous support. Their contributions not only provide medicines but also help build a resilient healthcare system in Liberia." ; She emphasized that these partnerships are crucial in achieving Liberia's long-term goal of universal healthcare access.

a3296.speaker: Li, Chinese Premier
a3296.name: Li
a3296.title: Chinese Premier
a3296.speech: Stressed the importance of increasing mutual strategic trust and strengthening cooperation in areas of common interest ; stressed that this milestone represents a key opportunity to strengthen ties and promote joint development, as a "knot that links the past to the future."

a3296.speaker: Xinhua (official Chinese news agency)
a3296.name: Xinhua (official Chinese news agency)
a3296.speech: Reported that the meeting focused on the need to strengthen understanding between China and the EU ahead of the 50th anniversary of their diplomatic relations, which will be commemorated next year.

a3296.speaker: China
a3296.name: China
a3296.speech: Expressed its intention to work with the EU not only to improve the well-being of its people, but also to contribute to world peace and development.

a3333.speaker: Ministry of Finance of Malawi
a3333.name: Ministry of Finance of Malawi
a3333.speech: Has set a medium-term objective of reducing the overall fiscal deficit to 6 percent of GDP, a target that hinges on sustained growth in revenue collections.

a3333.speaker: Malawian authorities
a3333.name: Malawian authorities
a3333.speech: Argue that the buoyancy seen in the 2024/25 fiscal year, which produced a 39.9 percent nominal increase in tax revenue over the previous year, will continue; they attribute this not only to reinforced tax policy measures, but also to administrative reforms that have begun to change how revenue is collected and enforced.

a3333.speaker: Gloria Zimba, Corporate Affairs Director, Castel Malawi
a3333.name: Gloria Zimba
a3333.title: Corporate Affairs Director, Castel Malawi
a3333.speech: Speaking to the press, urged consumers to avoid products lacking digital stamps, underscoring that compliance ensures the government can capture the revenue needed to invest in essential services and infrastructure: "The stamps allow the government to realize the correct amount of revenue to invest in essential social services development initiatives for economic growth."

a3333.speaker: Malawi Revenue Authority (MRA)
a3333.name: Malawi Revenue Authority (MRA)
a3333.speech: Confirmed in February 2025 that Kalondola had been fully linked with ASYCUDA, the customs management platform used at borders.

a3333.speaker: Wilma Chalulu, Acting Head of Corporate Affairs, Malawi Revenue Authority
a3333.name: Wilma Chalulu
a3333.title: Acting Head of Corporate Affairs, Malawi Revenue Authority
a3333.speech: "The implementation has successfully achieved one of its key objectives, ensuring that all import declarations for the specified tariff lines are accompanied by tax stamps" ; added that the integration had also improved operational efficiency by cutting redundancies in customs processes and boosting compliance among importers.

a3333.speaker: IMF report on Malawi's revenue mobilization strategy
a3333.name: IMF report on Malawi's revenue mobilization strategy
a3333.speech: Has emphasized the importance of such measures; the report recommended retaining excises on sectors such as gaming, gambling, airtime, and jewelry while sharpening enforcement against smuggling through prepaid tax stamps and closer monitoring of illicit trade; it further advised shifting from ad-valorem to specific excises on goods like alcohol, tobacco, and vehicles, aligning rates more closely with regional averages to reduce distortions and protect domestic industries.

a3333.speaker: Malawian authorities (as reported in the IMF report)
a3333.name: Malawian authorities (as reported in the IMF report)
a3333.speech: Argued that the combination of digital tax stamps, strengthened audits, enhanced VAT inspections, and intensified debt recovery would sustain the revenue buoyancy observed in FY2024/25.

a3354.speaker: World Food Programme (WFP)
a3354.name: World Food Programme (WFP)
a3354.speech: The UN agency reported that it suspended nutrition treatment for 650,000 women and children in Ethiopia this week due to a severe funding shortage; according to the WFP, more than 10 million people in Ethiopia suffer from severe food shortages, including 3 million displaced by conflict and extreme weather conditions, as well as refugees from war-devastated Sudan.

a3354.speaker: Zlatan Milisic, WFP Country Director in Ethiopia
a3354.name: Zlatan Milisic
a3354.title: WFP Country Director in Ethiopia
a3354.speech: Said the WFP receives funding from 15 to 20 donors, including the United States, however many of them cut funding this year; said the WFP had already cut rations in recent months, but that its operations were now at a "breaking point" due to the severe lack of funding, forcing more drastic measures.

a3354.speaker: Reuters
a3354.name: Reuters
a3354.speech: According to Reuters, the agency received exemptions from the humanitarian aid freeze imposed by American president Donald Trump, which halted humanitarian work throughout the world.

a3389.speaker: Roger Baro, Minister of the Environment, Water and Sanitation of Burkina Faso
a3389.name: Roger Baro
a3389.title: Minister of the Environment, Water and Sanitation of Burkina Faso
a3389.speech: Explained that the project for which the ALT gave its approval is a response to the national drinking water supply programme and to the security and humanitarian crisis; in the intervention zones it will alleviate difficulties of access to drinking water for a minimum of 174,000 people spread across 144 localities; indicated that, except for the Est and Sahel regions where other initiatives are under way, implementation in the 11 remaining areas of the country will translate into the execution of several infrastructures, the infrastructure component accounting for 91% of the budget ; "It is an investment project. We will have at least 50 high-flow boreholes, that is, more than 5 cubic metres of water per hour. This will make it possible to build 10 drinking water supply systems, 85 mini drinking water supply systems and nearly 95 water towers. These will not be individual systems, but rather collective ones." ; noted that one of the innovations of the project is the strengthening of the water trades centre of the National Water and Sanitation Office (ONEA), that the maintenance aspect of rural infrastructure must be taken into account and training will be initiated, and maintained that, over the project's 21 months from January 2024, his department is on the path to making the battle for water a reality in terms of access and availability.

a3389.speaker: Aminata Zerbo, Minister of Digital Transition, Posts and Electronic Communications of Burkina Faso
a3389.name: Aminata Zerbo
a3389.title: Minister of Digital Transition, Posts and Electronic Communications of Burkina Faso
a3389.speech: Provided clarifications on certain points of the bill on the security of information systems and took into account the deputies' amendments and concerns; after the adoption of the law, declared that it had been long awaited, given the evolution of digital technology and the government's drive to make digital technology a lever for economic development through the dematerialisation of administrative procedures, with services now accessible online; added that the government has put fairly sensitive data online ; "We are exposing ourselves in a certain way. These services and data are accessible to users, but also to malicious people who might perhaps want to harm our country. They can attack these services. It is important for us to put in place everything needed in terms of mechanisms to better secure our cyberspace, the information system and digital assets," she explained ; said the law is one of the key pieces in having a regulatory framework allowing better control and surveillance of cyberspace and supervision of all operators of information systems, enabling periodic audits, special protection of critical infrastructure and regulation of the import and sale of equipment and software ; "It is a law that we are making available to the national agency for the security of information systems and the other actors of the digital ecosystem so as to better ensure the protection of our cyberspace," she concluded.

a3389.speaker: Deputies of the Transitional Legislative Assembly (ALT) of Burkina Faso
a3389.name: Deputies of the Transitional Legislative Assembly (ALT) of Burkina Faso
a3389.speech: Adopted the two bills, authorising the financing for carrying out the PAEP-LF project works for the benefit of the populations; on the information systems security bill they expressed their concerns through questions linked to new advances in the digital field and the protection of the State's information systems.

a3541.speaker: “State of the Economy” report, National Economic Council of Somalia
a3541.name: “State of the Economy” report
a3541.title: National Economic Council of Somalia
a3541.speech: Reported that Somalia’s economy is showing signs of resilience with notable progress in key sectors, growing by 4.2% in 2023 from 2.7% the previous year, with agriculture contributing 65% of GDP led by livestock exports; that mobile money platforms serve over 81.8% of the population; that external debt fell from 64% of GDP in 2018 to under 6% by 2023 under the HIPC Initiative and domestic revenues surged by 25%, while a fiscal deficit of 0.3% persists and public spending reached $720.3 million in 2023; that imports ballooned to $7.4 billion while exports stagnated at $861 million; and that over half the population lives below the poverty line (an improvement from 69% in 2021), 3.8 million people face acute food shortages, youth unemployment stands at 30.1%, and formal banking services remain out of reach for 91% of Somalis.

a3541.speaker: Hassan Adam Hosow, Chief Economic Advisor to the President and Executive Director of the National Economic Council
a3541.name: Hassan Adam Hosow
a3541.title: Chief Economic Advisor to the President and Executive Director of the National Economic Council
a3541.speech: Emphasized the importance of sustaining this momentum through targeted policies: “The primary goal is to take stock of key developments in our economy and establish a tradition where Somalia speaks for itself in terms of economic development. It’s not just about accounting for effects but understanding why they happen and addressing gaps with effective policies. Where we see positive developments, we aim to lock them in, and where there are missed opportunities, we propose interventions to close those gaps” ; described the annual report as a critical tool for the government designed to provide actionable insights and solutions to guide economic policy: “This is only our second annual report, but it’s already become a cornerstone for evaluating Somalia’s economic trajectory.”

a3541.speaker: Hassan Adam Hosow, Chief Economic Advisor to the President and Executive Director of the National Economic Council
a3541.name: Hassan Adam Hosow
a3541.title: Chief Economic Advisor to the President and Executive Director of the National Economic Council
a3541.speech: Outlined ambitious long-term plans for Somalia’s economic transformation: “Somalia is working on two key frameworks: the Centennial Vision 2060, aligned with Africa’s Agenda 2063, and the National Transformation Plan, which marks the first phase of this vision. The Centennial Vision aims to ensure Somalia reaches middle-income status by its 100th birthday” ; “We aim to preserve traditional economic pillars like agriculture, livestock, and fisheries while thinking long-term about transforming Somalia’s coastline into a logistics hub.”

a3541.speaker: Hassan Adam Hosow, Chief Economic Advisor to the President and Executive Director of the National Economic Council
a3541.name: Hassan Adam Hosow
a3541.title: Chief Economic Advisor to the President and Executive Director of the National Economic Council
a3541.speech: Highlighted factors driving modest economic growth, including improved security, financial reforms, and the absence of major droughts: “What ties all this together is sound macroeconomic policy,” emphasizing the need for sustained reforms, strategic investments, and regional collaboration to unlock Somalia’s immense potential for long-term stability and prosperity.

a3541.speaker: National Economic Council of Somalia
a3541.name: National Economic Council of Somalia
a3541.speech: Recommends strengthening fiscal systems by establishing the Somalia Revenue Agency, promoting trade diversification in fisheries and light manufacturing, expanding financial inclusion through mobile money interoperability and microfinance initiatives, and investing in renewable energy and sustainable agriculture as essential to mitigating climate risks; the report also calls for long-term investments in education, healthcare, and climate resilience to break the cycle of poverty.

a3613.speaker: Joseph Boakai, President of Liberia
a3613.name: Joseph Boakai
a3613.title: President of Liberia
a3613.speech: Disclosed Liberia’s qualification to acquire a second compact grant from the Millennium Challenge Corporation (MCC): “Liberia’s qualification is predicated upon the significant improvements made by the Liberian Government in the governance process of the country.” ; Described the news as a giant achievement in the history of Liberia, which will further help to address the binding constraints to growth, and said it will also unlock the country’s untapped natural resources as the government remains keen on bettering the lives of the citizens through its developmental plans.

a3613.speaker: Joseph Boakai, President of Liberia
a3613.name: Joseph Boakai
a3613.title: President of Liberia
a3613.speech: Urged all citizens to unite in the face of adversity: “Liberia, as a nation, is stronger when citizens from all sides unite in fostering national growth and development.” ; Encouraged citizens to do away with vices that tend to derail the progress of the country and embrace the spirit of peaceful coexistence and national healing, and reaffirmed the government’s commitment to upholding democracy, the rule of law, and the principles of good governance.

a3720.speaker: Alexander Kofi-Mensah Mould, Chief Executive Officer of the Millennium Development Authority (MiDA)
a3720.name: Alexander Kofi-Mensah Mould
a3720.title: Chief Executive Officer of the Millennium Development Authority (MiDA)
a3720.speech: Assured local and international investors that projects under Ghana’s 24-Hour Economy and Accelerated Export Development (24H+) initiative are not only viable but built on strong foundations of transparency and accountability; emphasised that these projects are “bankable” and explained that each project has undergone thorough vetting, backed by feasibility studies, clear regulatory frameworks, and well-structured risk mitigation strategies ; “Bankability means that investor capital is protected and expected to yield returns. We’re not just offering ideas — we’re presenting executable, results-driven projects.” ; reminded the audience of the Authority’s successful delivery of over $1.1 billion worth of multi-sector projects across infrastructure, energy, and agriculture, all funded by the U.S. Millennium Challenge Corporation: “We did it under some of the world’s most rigorous standards. Now, we’re ready to do it again — faster, better, and smarter.” ; emphasised that for Ghana to realise its economic ambitions, capable and transparent institutions must take the lead: “That’s what MiDA brings to the table — a proven track record, executional rigor, and the ability to turn policy into real-world impact.”

a3720.speaker: Participants (capital market operators at the roundtable)
a3720.name: Participants (capital market operators at the roundtable)
a3720.speech: Cited challenges such as corruption in procurement processes, political interference in contract execution, and the historical pattern of discontinuing development projects after changes in government.

a3720.speaker: Augustus Obuadum Tanoh, Presidential Adviser on the 24-Hour Economy and Accelerated Export Development
a3720.name: Augustus Obuadum Tanoh
a3720.title: Presidential Adviser on the 24-Hour Economy and Accelerated Export Development
a3720.speech: Outlined how the initiative intends to leverage capital markets to fund the country’s ambitious plans; said the roundtable focused on key enablers such as mobilizing both domestic and foreign investments, managing risks associated with extended operational hours, and ensuring long-term sustainability of the policy ; “The 24-hour economy isn’t just about more work, it’s about smarter economic structuring that fuels job creation, supports infrastructure, and drives export-oriented growth.”

a3720.speaker: Nana Dwemoh Benneh, Chief Executive of the Ghana Infrastructure Investment Fund (GIIF)
a3720.name: Nana Dwemoh Benneh
a3720.title: Chief Executive of the Ghana Infrastructure Investment Fund (GIIF)
a3720.speech: Emphasized that regular progress reports, covering project milestones, financial performance, and alignment with strategic goals, will be shared with stakeholders; added that independent external auditors will review GIIF’s financial activities, alongside impact assessments to measure how investments are driving infrastructure development across the country.

a3875.speaker: Rotary Club of Accra Ridge
a3875.name: Rotary Club of Accra Ridge
a3875.speech: At the inauguration ceremony held in Accra, the club announced plans to raise over GH¢300,000 to promote mental health awareness and support community-based projects in Accra and beyond.

a3875.speaker: Oppong Agyare Agyeman-Anane, new President of the Rotary Club of Accra Ridge
a3875.name: Oppong Agyare Agyeman-Anane
a3875.title: new President of the Rotary Club of Accra Ridge
a3875.speech: Emphasised the importance of teamwork and active member participation; encouraged Rotarians to support the Rotary Foundation by paying dues promptly, attending meetings and project events, and contributing positively to club activities; also called for increased donations to the PolioPlus Fund to support global efforts towards polio eradication.

a3875.speaker: Efosa Aibangbee, outgoing President of the Rotary Club of Accra Ridge
a3875.name: Efosa Aibangbee
a3875.title: outgoing President of the Rotary Club of Accra Ridge
a3875.speech: Highlighted achievements during his tenure, including growth in club membership and support for the Nii Amugi Cluster of Schools in Accra; he also noted significant progress on the Mallam Atta Delivery and Maternity Unit Clinic, which is nearing completion.

a3875.speaker: Nana Yaa Pokua Siriboe, District Governor
a3875.name: Nana Yaa Pokua Siriboe
a3875.title: District Governor
a3875.speech: Urged Rotarians and well-wishers to continue supporting the work of The Rotary Foundation; she expressed confidence that the new leadership team would build on the club’s achievements and continue to make a positive impact in society.

a3920.speaker: Dr Iziaq Adekunle Salako, Minister of State for Environment
a3920.name: Dr Iziaq Adekunle Salako
a3920.title: Minister of State for Environment
a3920.speech: Has said air pollution is the second leading risk factor for premature deaths resulting in around 8.1 million deaths annually, stressing that “This is more than the deaths associated with malaria and HIV combined”, speaking at the weekend during an event to mark the second International Day of Clean Air for Blue Skies in Abuja.

a3920.speaker: Dr Iziaq Adekunle Salako, Minister of State for Environment
a3920.name: Dr Iziaq Adekunle Salako
a3920.title: Minister of State for Environment
a3920.speech: Said research had confirmed that air pollution was directly linked to dementia and Alzheimer's disease aside from being responsible for ailments such as stroke, heart disease, lung cancer, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease and acute respiratory infections; and said there is a growing concern globally about air pollution and the threat poor air posed to human existence.

a3920.speaker: Dr Iziaq Adekunle Salako, Minister of State for Environment
a3920.name: Dr Iziaq Adekunle Salako
a3920.title: Minister of State for Environment
a3920.speech: “Beyond the direct adverse effect on health, air pollution from greenhouse gases, Short Lived Climate Pollutants (SCLPs), black carbon and so on are at the core of global warming, which is the driver of climate change, climate disasters with loss of lives, food insecurity, economic losses, migration and physical insecurity challenges.”

a3920.speaker: Dr Iziaq Adekunle Salako, Minister of State for Environment
a3920.name: Dr Iziaq Adekunle Salako
a3920.title: Minister of State for Environment
a3920.speech: Said their agenda is to reduce all forms of air pollutants to 50 per cent globally by 2030, adding that Nigeria is faced with significant air pollution challenges and was ranked the 3rd most polluted country in Africa by the 2021 world air quality report: “In 2023, the average PM2.5 concentration in Nigeria was 4.8 times of the World Health Organisation's annual air quality guideline value. Like most parts of the world, vehicular emission is the greatest contributor to air pollution, with the situation complicated in our country by the many old, second hand, third hand, in fact several hand automobiles plying our roads. Other sources include industrial activities, illegal refining, gas flaring, burning of refuse, household cooking and power generation.”

a3920.speaker: Dr Iziaq Adekunle Salako, Minister of State for Environment
a3920.name: Dr Iziaq Adekunle Salako
a3920.title: Minister of State for Environment
a3920.speech: Maintained that if they failed to take action and reverse the current high level of air pollution in the country and in the world, the repercussions for public health, economy, environment and their survival is far reaching: “The issue of vehicular emission is a major area that we need to deal with in improving our air quality. Government will continue to put measures in place, including appropriate tariffs and taxes, to discourage the importation of old and rickety vehicles, encourage local manufacturing and assembling of vehicles.”

a3920.speaker: Dr Iziaq Adekunle Salako, Minister of State for Environment
a3920.name: Dr Iziaq Adekunle Salako
a3920.title: Minister of State for Environment
a3920.speech: Said the ministry, through its regulatory/enforcement agencies and in collaboration with other MDAs, is working to improve the quality of air being inhaled by Nigerians using multifaceted policy instruments, legislations, programmes and projects, and is working to establish a national framework to guide states setting up vehicular and generator Emissions Testing Centres in line with minimum standards developed by NESREA and the Standards Organization of Nigeria: “We are determined to ensure that vehicular and generator emission testings are not just about revenue but about compliance with National Ambient air quality standards.”

a3920.speaker: Mahmud Kambari, Permanent Secretary (represented by Mariya Rufai, Director of Human Resources)
a3920.name: Mahmud Kambari
a3920.title: Permanent Secretary (represented by Mariya Rufai, Director of Human Resources)
a3920.speech: Said the elders, women and children are more vulnerable to air pollution and thus the need to ensure clean air, which is a great enabler for good health; said there is need to embark on wider sensitisation towards enlightening the people of the consequences of air pollution: “Climate change issues can be reduced to the barest minimum if we have quality air.”

a3920.speaker: 2021 World Air Quality Report
a3920.name: 2021 World Air Quality Report
a3920.speech: Ranked Nigeria the 3rd most polluted country in Africa.

a4258.speaker: Rick Dzida, economic expert
a4258.name: Rick Dzida
a4258.title: economic expert
a4258.speech: In a lecture, outlined the disadvantages of currency devaluation: that devaluation increases import prices, leading to higher production costs and consumer prices, fuelling inflation and reducing purchasing power; that it may not necessarily increase exports, as other countries may retaliate with their own devaluations; that it can trigger capital flight and discourage foreign investment; that socially it exacerbates poverty, unemployment and social unrest; and that politically it erodes public trust in the government's economic management, limits independent economic policy and increases reliance on foreign aid and loans.

a4258.speaker: Rick Dzida, economic expert
a4258.name: Rick Dzida
a4258.title: economic expert
a4258.speech: Proposes several mitigating strategies: diversifying exports, improving productivity, reducing dependence on imports, implementing fiscal discipline, maintaining monetary policy credibility, building foreign exchange reserves, currency hedging, inflation targeting, supply-side reforms and effective communication from policymakers, as well as industry-specific strategies in agriculture, manufacturing and services.

a4258.speaker: Simplex Chithyola Banda, Malawi's Minister of Finance
a4258.name: Simplex Chithyola Banda
a4258.title: Malawi's Minister of Finance
a4258.speech: Has acknowledged the impact of devaluation on Malawi's economy, stating that the country will have to make tough decisions to recover.

a4258.speaker: European Union
a4258.name: European Union
a4258.speech: Has also provided support, pledging 60 million Euros to help Malawi's economy.

a4372.speaker: Government of South Africa
a4372.name: Government of South Africa
a4372.speech: Said it will not allow the removal of approximately 427 million dollars (1.1 trillion shillings) that was being provided by the United States to weaken its major programme for fighting HIV infections.

a4372.speaker: AP News
a4372.name: AP News
a4372.speech: According to AP News, the programme, though large, faces challenges, with health experts warning that in the next few years the country could witness thousands of new infections.

a4372.speaker: Yvette Raphael, co-founder of Advocacy for Prevention of HIV and AIDS (South Africa)
a4372.name: Yvette Raphael
a4372.title: co-founder of Advocacy for Prevention of HIV and AIDS (South Africa)
a4372.speech: Said the situation of fear will continue if the government does not undertake a process to fight the disease: “We fear that we will see the number of people living with HIV increase greatly. We are worried about the number of children who will be born with the infection because of the shortage of services. The money we were receiving from USAid was covering a gap that our government could not solve.”

a4372.speaker: Patient who did not want her name mentioned (anonymous), South Africa
a4372.name: Patient who did not want her name mentioned (anonymous)
a4372.title: South Africa
a4372.speech: “Our lives matter, we are human beings, those clinics were important to us for treatment. The financial support was important in our lives. The clinic would come to my house, giving me services there. It would check on me every three months and give me medicine.” ; quoted by AP News she added, “I only needed to go to the clinic for medicine as well; whenever I needed a condom or lubricants it would provide them to me.”

a4372.speaker: People collecting medicine at various centres in South Africa
a4372.name: People collecting medicine at various centres in South Africa
a4372.speech: Said the financial support that was being provided by the United States was very important in their lives.

a4372.speaker: Trump government (United States)
a4372.name: Trump government (United States)
a4372.speech: Defended itself by saying that the spending did not align with the interests of the United States.

a4372.speaker: Russell Vought, Director of the U.S. Office of Management and Budget
a4372.name: Russell Vought
a4372.title: Director of the U.S. Office of Management and Budget
a4372.speech: Said at an advisory session in June this year: “We have a debt of 37 trillion dollars, equal to 93 trillion shillings. So, at some point, the African continent should bear more of the burden of providing these health services.”

a4372.speaker: Some South African citizens
a4372.name: Some South African citizens
a4372.speech: Say that Trump’s stance may be influenced by the American of South African origin, Elon Musk, who was associated with the earlier efforts to cut US aid.

a4433.speaker: International Court of Justice (ICJ) (order of 24 May 2024)
a4433.name: International Court of Justice (ICJ) (order of 24 May 2024)
