a4433.speech: Ordered Israel to halt “immediately” its military offensive in Rafah because of the immediate risk to the Palestinian people; underlined in its order that “the catastrophic humanitarian situation in the Gaza Strip, which it had noted in its order of 26 January 2024 was at serious risk of deteriorating, has since deteriorated, and even more so since it delivered its order of 28 March 2024”; considered these developments constitute “a change in the situation within the meaning of Article 76 of the Rules” and that “the immense risks associated with a military offensive in Rafah have begun to materialise, and will increase further if the operation continues”; reaffirmed by 13 votes to two the provisional measures of 26 January and 28 March 2024; indicated by 13 votes to two that Israel must “immediately halt its military offensive, and any other action in the Rafah Governorate, which may inflict on the Palestinian group in Gaza conditions of life that could bring about its physical destruction in whole or in part”, must “maintain open the Rafah crossing for unimpeded provision at scale of urgently needed basic services and humanitarian assistance”, must “take effective measures to ensure the unimpeded access to the Gaza Strip of any commission of inquiry, fact-finding mission or other investigative body mandated by competent organs of the United Nations to investigate allegations of genocide”, and must submit a report to the Court on all measures taken to give effect to the order within one month.

a4433.speaker: Karim Khan, Prosecutor of the International Criminal Court (ICC)
a4433.name: Karim Khan
a4433.title: Prosecutor of the International Criminal Court (ICC)
a4433.speech: Requested arrest warrants against Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, his Defence Minister Yoav Gallant, and three Hamas leaders, for alleged crimes committed in Gaza and in Israel.

a4433.speaker: Antonio Guterres, UN Secretary-General (via spokesperson Stéphane Dujarric)
a4433.name: Antonio Guterres
a4433.title: UN Secretary-General (via spokesperson Stéphane Dujarric)
a4433.speech: Announced he had taken note of the ICJ order: “The Secretary-General recalls that, in accordance with the Charter and the Statute of the Court, the decisions of the International Court of Justice are binding and he trusts that the parties will duly comply with the Court’s order” ; “In accordance with the Statute of the Court, the Secretary-General will also transmit as soon as possible to the Security Council the notification of the provisional measures ordered by the Court.”

a4433.speaker: Vusimuzi Madonsela, South African ambassador to the Netherlands
a4433.name: Vusimuzi Madonsela
a4433.title: South African ambassador to the Netherlands
a4433.speech: Declared on 16 May that his country was compelled to return before the Court by virtue of its obligations under the Genocide Convention “because of the continuing annihilation of the Palestinian people, with more than 35,000 dead and most of Gaza reduced to ruins”.

a4433.speaker: Vaughn Lowe, of the group of lawyers and experts presenting South Africa’s arguments
a4433.name: Vaughn Lowe
a4433.title: of the group of lawyers and experts presenting South Africa’s arguments
a4433.speech: “The key point today is that Israel’s declared objective of wiping Gaza off the map is on the verge of being achieved” ; “The evidence of appalling crimes and atrocities is literally being destroyed and bulldozed, which wipes the slate clean for those who committed these crimes and makes a mockery of justice.”

a4433.speaker: Gilad Noam, co-agent of Israel
a4433.name: Gilad Noam
a4433.title: co-agent of Israel
a4433.speech: Appearing before the Court on 17 May, refuted South Africa’s claims, describing them as an “obscene exploitation” of the “most sacred” Genocide Convention; declared that Israel was engaged in a “difficult and tragic” armed conflict, a fact essential to “understanding the situation” but ignored by South Africa: “This makes a mockery of the heinous charge of genocide… facts matter and truth should matter. Words must keep their meaning. Calling something genocide over and over again does not make it genocide.”

a4433.speaker: South Africa (application filed with the ICJ)
a4433.name: South Africa (application filed with the ICJ)
a4433.speech: Filed an application on 10 May seeking an order requiring Israel to cease immediately all its military operations and to facilitate access to humanitarian aid; on 29 December 2023 had filed an application instituting proceedings against Israel over alleged violations of the Genocide Convention, with a request for provisional measures to “protect against further, severe and irreparable harm to the rights of the Palestinian people under the Genocide Convention” and calling for “Israel’s compliance with its obligations under the Convention not to commit genocide, and to prevent and to punish genocide”.

a4479.speaker: Representative of the CEO of Malbaza Cement Company (MCC)
a4479.name: Representative of the CEO of Malbaza Cement Company (MCC)
a4479.speech: Explained to the ministerial delegation that since the entry into force of the reduction in the price of cement, the company has produced more than 50,000 tonnes of 32.5 cement, and that, faced with growing demand from the population, the company has revised its programme, moving to 90% production of 32.5 cement and 10% of 42.5 cement ; set out the energy difficulties preventing the company's development ; reiterated MCC's commitment to ensuring the supply of 32.5 cement to the market.

a4479.speaker: Seydou Asman, Minister of Trade and Industry of Niger
a4479.name: Seydou Asman
a4479.title: Minister of Trade and Industry of Niger
a4479.speech: Indicated that he had wanted to make this visit following the measure taken by the State to reduce the price of 32.5 cement, in order to hear first-hand the concerns of the staff regarding the consequences of that measure ; affirmed that the measure is to make cement accessible to the population and that on this measure the State will not waver ; encouraged the company for having maintained the smooth running of the business and asked its managers to recruit and create jobs for young people.

a4479.speaker: Seydou Asman, Minister of Trade and Industry of Niger
a4479.name: Seydou Asman
a4479.title: Minister of Trade and Industry of Niger
a4479.speech: Said he had come to see for himself how the distribution of cement is being carried out since the signing of the ordinance reducing the price of cement in Niger: “we have observed on all sides a sort of shortage that dares not speak its name, according to the information we are receiving”, explaining that he had been instructed by the country's highest authorities “to come and see what is happening exactly” ; specified that “the factories are operating normally” and that there is a significant number of trucks that should serve to supply the country ; “What is very unfortunate is to observe a shortage or a lack of cement” in the country ; warned that “in any event, investigations will be carried out among the producers and approved distributors, and sanctions will be taken against offenders” ; reassured Nigeriens that “everything will return to order” and called on consumers to report violations and on the population to take part so that the price-reduction measure produces a result.

a4479.speaker: Colonel-Major Oumarou Tawayé, Governor of the Tahoua Region
a4479.name: Colonel-Major Oumarou Tawayé
a4479.title: Governor of the Tahoua Region
a4479.speech: After congratulating the company, focused his remarks on the safety of quarries, the environment, and the payment of royalties to the municipalities.

a4694.speaker: Bintou Keita, UN Special Envoy
a4694.name: Bintou Keita
a4694.title: UN Special Envoy
a4694.speech: In a recent address to the Security Council, highlighted the progress made in recent months, including a ceasefire between DRC and Rwanda and increased dialogue between the two countries ; while acknowledging the persistence of violence, expressed hope for a peaceful resolution.

a4694.speaker: Bintou Keita, UN Special Envoy
a4694.name: Bintou Keita
a4694.title: UN Special Envoy
a4694.speech: Emphasized the need for continued humanitarian assistance to address the dire situation facing millions of displaced people in the region ; called on the international community to provide adequate funding to support the most vulnerable populations.

a4887.speaker: USAID Demographic and Health Survey (latest survey)
a4887.name: USAID Demographic and Health Survey (latest survey)
a4887.speech: According to the latest demographic and health survey carried out by USAID, Benin still has a contraceptive prevalence rate of 7.9%, placing it among the countries of the sub-region where the rate of use of modern family planning methods remains low.

a4887.speaker: Michael Raynor, U.S. Ambassador to Benin
a4887.name: Michael Raynor
a4887.title: U.S. Ambassador to Benin
a4887.speech: said the project provides clear messages on the economic and health benefits of families with well-spaced births. “Family planning can improve people’s lives, for example through increased personal income, reduced maternal mortality and greater investment in children’s education.” He also reaffirmed the commitment of the United States of America to continue its actions in favour of the well-being of the Beninese population.

a4887.speaker: Dorothée Kindé Gazard, Minister of Health of Benin
a4887.name: Dorothée Kindé Gazard
a4887.title: Minister of Health of Benin
a4887.speech: expressed great satisfaction with the various actions accomplished in implementing the project and commended all the actors involved; she said she remains more convinced than ever that the advocacy tool will contribute to achieving Millennium Development Goals 1 and 3.

a4887.speaker: Marcel de-Souza, Minister of Development, Economic Analysis and Forecasting of Benin
a4887.name: Marcel de-Souza
a4887.title: Minister of Development, Economic Analysis and Forecasting of Benin
a4887.speech: praised the development project made available to the Beninese people, saying the importance of family planning no longer needs to be demonstrated today. “It is a key strategy for promoting the health and survival of women and children, reducing poverty and fostering economic growth both nationally and at the family level.”

a4889.speaker: Dr. Matthew Opoku Prempeh (NAPO), former Member of Parliament for Manhyia South
a4889.name: Dr. Matthew Opoku Prempeh (NAPO)
a4889.title: former Member of Parliament for Manhyia South
a4889.speech: affirmed his commitment to empowering the youth and artisans through skills development; speaking under the theme “Empowering Hands, Elevating Dreams: Crafting Ghana’s Future”, he emphasised the critical role of vocational skills in nation-building. According to him, the future of Ghana will not be written by what we import, but by what we build with our own hands, stressing that skills are not alternatives, but the foundation of national greatness.

a4889.speaker: Nana Agyei Baffuor Awuah, current Manhyia South MP
a4889.name: Nana Agyei Baffuor Awuah
a4889.title: current Manhyia South MP
a4889.speech: commended Dr Opoku Prempeh for the laudable initiative and described it as a legacy that would help reduce unemployment and criminal activities within the Constituency. He promised to ensure that the initiative is sustained to benefit more youth, especially those interested in the apprenticeship.

a4889.speaker: Nana Apau Wiafe Ababio Sanwoansan, Chief of Kwabre Heman
a4889.name: Nana Apau Wiafe Ababio Sanwoansan
a4889.title: Chief of Kwabre Heman
a4889.speech: commended the Members of Parliament for the initiative towards reducing unemployment and job creation to reduce criminal activities and immoral lifestyle among the youth, especially in the Manhyia South constituency. He also entreated the Shoemakers to consider going into making royal (ahenemma) sandals, also known as ‘kyawkyaw’ for festive occasions, besides funerals and other occasions, and advised them to take the profession seriously because it is their life and future.

a4967.speaker: Saboi Imboela, National Democratic Congress (NDC) leader
a4967.name: Saboi Imboela
a4967.title: National Democratic Congress (NDC) leader
a4967.speech: Has challenged the Anti-Corruption Commission (ACC) to seriously investigate the 650,000 metric tonnes of maize being imported from Tanzania, from which reports are to the effect that only 14,000 metric tonnes have been delivered from the 200,000 tonnes which was paid for; said in an interview yesterday that the importation of the 650,000 metric tonnes of maize from Tanzania was one of the latest corruption scandals and that the ACC should investigate.

a4967.speaker: Saboi Imboela, National Democratic Congress (NDC) leader
a4967.name: Saboi Imboela
a4967.title: National Democratic Congress (NDC) leader
a4967.speech: Says it is disheartening that Rueben Mtolo Phiri, the Minister of Agriculture, has refused to inform the nation about what was happening to the 650,000 metric tonnes of maize being imported from Tanzania.

a4996.speaker: McMillan Anyanwu, African Development Bank (AfDB) country manager for Malawi
a4996.name: McMillan Anyanwu
a4996.title: African Development Bank (AfDB) country manager for Malawi
a4996.speech: Said the $23 million (about K40 billion) agriculture-based budgetary support programme is designed to unlock the agriculture sector's potential as a catalyst for economic transformation: "The direct budget support will target key reforms to protect the well-being of people in rural and vulnerable communities. We believe that these reforms will help Malawi realise its dream of becoming a net-exporter of value-added products."

a4996.speaker: McMillan Anyanwu, African Development Bank (AfDB) country manager for Malawi
a4996.name: McMillan Anyanwu
a4996.title: African Development Bank (AfDB) country manager for Malawi
a4996.speech: Said the Africa Disaster Risk Financing (Adrifi) programme is designed to strengthen the country's resilience by improving disaster planning and crisis response capabilities, particularly for rural farming communities that are most at risk.

a4996.speaker: Simplex Chithyola-Banda, Malawi Minister of Finance and Economic Affairs
a4996.name: Simplex Chithyola-Banda
a4996.title: Malawi Minister of Finance and Economic Affairs
a4996.speech: Commended AfDB for providing the support, saying it complements the Malawi 2063 long-term development plan which earmarked agriculture productivity and commercialisation as key pillars for promoting economic transformation: "This budgetary support will help create an enabling economic and regulatory environment for agricultural transformation by promoting agricultural productivity, commercialisation and market access to help our farmers increase their output and connect to better markets."

a5003.speaker: Fitch Ratings Agency
a5003.name: Fitch Ratings Agency
a5003.speech: Believes that the suspension of support from the United States Agency for International Development (USAID) to Mozambique has contributed to the shortage of foreign currency (particularly of US dollars); according to a recent publication, USAID disbursements represented approximately three percent of Mozambique's Gross Domestic Product "as a result of an investment, on average, between 250 million and 300 million dollars per year" ; "The Agency's withdrawal not only left more than 2,500 people unemployed but also worsened the country's economic situation, as its presence accounted for up to three per cent of the GDP. The shortage of foreign currency increased in 2025, in part due to the decline in external disbursements to the Government and the suspension of USAID."

a5003.speaker: Fitch Ratings Agency
a5003.name: Fitch Ratings Agency
a5003.speech: According to the document, the country's large financing needs pose a significant vulnerability although switch auctions on local-currency bonds, central bank borrowing, and short-term financing are being used to service debt: "The foreign exchange reserves have held up, but external disbursements have declined, which coupled with challenging domestic financing, increases risks of spillover to external repayments. Mozambique's fiscal deficit widened to 4.9 per cent of GDP in 2024, from 2.1 per cent in 2023, mostly reflecting a decline in grants and some impact from the post-election violence on revenue collection." ; However, the Agency expects that the country's fiscal deficit "will narrow to 3.4 per cent of GDP in 2025 and a forecast 3.6 per cent in 2026, mostly driven by falling expenditure. Financing constraints will contain capex, and we anticipate the public sector wage bill will fall relative to GDP. Nevertheless, budget rigidities will remain significant."

a5003.speaker: Fitch Ratings Agency
a5003.name: Fitch Ratings Agency
a5003.speech: Also says that the government accumulated, over the last year, external arrears to several bilateral and multilateral creditors (including the IMF, Portugal and the Islamic Development Bank): "In many instances, payments were only resolved after their specified grace period had elapsed. Fitch did not consider these incidents as defaults, as external commercial debt was not affected. Fitch understands that the accumulation of external arrears to the official sector has continued in 2025. The accumulation of arrears on domestic bonds also remains an issue, with the time for resolution of these delays having increased."

a5107.speaker: IPC (Integrated Food Security Phase Classification) Initiative
a5107.name: IPC (Integrated Food Security Phase Classification) Initiative
a5107.speech: According to the IPC initiative, which monitors extreme hunger worldwide, more than 24.6 million people, half of Sudan's population, are suffering from high-level acute food insecurity.

a5107.speaker: IPC Famine Review Committee
a5107.name: IPC Famine Review Committee
a5107.speech: Confirmed that famine (IPC Phase 5) is present in at least five areas, notably the Zamzam camp in North Darfur and parts of the western Nuba Mountains.

a5107.speaker: IPC report
a5107.name: IPC report
a5107.speech: “Famine is the most extreme manifestation of human suffering, representing a catastrophic collapse of the systems and resources essential to survival” ; “It is not simply a lack of food, but a profound degradation of health, livelihoods and social structures, leaving entire communities in a state of despair.”

a5107.speaker: IPC report
a5107.name: IPC report
a5107.speech: According to the report, farmers have been forced to abandon their fields and crops have been looted or destroyed; displaced families, particularly those living in encampments and public buildings, remain deprived of the benefits of the harvest.

a5107.speaker: IPC report
a5107.name: IPC report
a5107.speech: Stressed that only an immediate cessation of hostilities can prevent the worsening of the crisis. It calls for the restoration of safe, unhindered and sustained humanitarian access, particularly in conflict zones, and for a considerable scaling-up of multisectoral humanitarian aid; it also calls for scaling up the treatment of acute malnutrition, providing essential agricultural inputs to help vulnerable households meet their needs, and conducting food security and nutrition surveys in unassessed areas to refine response efforts.

a5132.speaker: A. Blamo Dixon, Resident Judge of Criminal Court “C”
a5132.name: A. Blamo Dixon
a5132.title: Resident Judge of Criminal Court “C”
a5132.speech: Issued a Writ of Subpoena Decu Tecum and Ad Testificandum on Col. Kromah on Wednesday, October 2, 2024, requiring him to testify in the US$31,625 drugs case; the court also subpoenaed the LDEA Officer in Charge Christopher Peter to appear on Thursday, October 3, along with CCTV footage taken from the home of one of the defendants, George Obi alias Japan.

a5132.speaker: Defense lawyers for the accused
a5132.name: Defense lawyers for the accused
a5132.speech: Made a motion requesting that Mr. Kromah testify on behalf of the defendants before the court on Friday, October 4, 2024; according to them, the request is to have Col. Kromah produce evidence regarding the case and testify on his role and on behalf of the defendants.

a5132.speaker: Liberia Drug Enforcement Agency (LDEA) investigation
a5132.name: Liberia Drug Enforcement Agency (LDEA) investigation
a5132.speech: According to the LDEA investigation, the value of the drugs discovered in Saryon Town, Logan Town on Bushrod Island is put at US$31,625 or its equivalent of LD$6,077,370.00.

a5132.speaker: Grand Jury of Montserrado County (indictment)
a5132.name: Grand Jury of Montserrado County (indictment)
a5132.speech: Indicted George Obi, Peter Mamah, Edwin Ozioko, Ndubuis Okornkwo, Igwe David, Sunday Udeh, Shelly, Shelton, Evan Jamo, China Ekwa, Edwin Ozioko, and Bridgestone Harris, among others, on charges of unlawful maintenance and distribution of controlled drugs or substances, unlicensed sale and distribution of controlled drugs or substances, and criminal conspiracy. The indictment said the defendants, being in the know of the harmfulness of these drugs to the growth and development of the country, went on to sell them; the Grand Jury said the defendants had the intent to pollute Liberia's youthful population and began to purposely, knowingly, wilfully, and intentionally transport, distribute, and sell these drugs to the detriment of Liberian society.

a5177.speaker: Food and Agriculture Organisation (FAO) of the United Nations, March 2021 crop prospects and food situation quarterly global report
a5177.name: Food and Agriculture Organisation (FAO) of the United Nations
a5177.title: March 2021 crop prospects and food situation quarterly global report
a5177.speech: Estimated that 441 000 Namibians are food insecure and would be in need of humanitarian assistance between October 2020 and March 2021, and stated that Namibia is among the 45 countries in need of external assistance for food. The report said in Namibia there are shortfalls in staple food production, which have been exacerbated by the economic slowdown, which in turn was worsened by the Covid-19 pandemic. “Although the availability of food is adequate and stable, the negative effects of the Covid-19 pandemic, primarily income and job losses, have constrained households' access to food,” reads the report. It also noted that FAO's production outlook for Botswana, eSwatini, Lesotho and Namibia is favourable owing to good rains; that in South Africa wholesale prices of maize grain increased in January 2021 and were more than 20% above their year-earlier levels; that in the import-dependent countries prices of maize meal were mostly stable in the last quarter of 2020 but higher than the previous year amid increasing import costs; and that aggregate cereal production by the 51 low-income food-deficit countries rose 3% in 2020 to 502.4 million tonnes while aggregate cereal import requirements in 2020/21 are expected to rise to 74.1 million tonnes.

a5177.speaker: Percy Misika, Executive Director in the Namibian Ministry of Agriculture
a5177.name: Percy Misika
a5177.title: Executive Director in the Namibian Ministry of Agriculture
a5177.speech: Said figures from the report refer to the lean period or the season starting from October 2020, when the harvest for the 2019/2020 cropping season was expected to have been depleted up to March 2021. “With the measures undertaken to ensure farmers have access to subsidised ploughing, planting and weeding services, coupled with the provision of subsidised seeds and the reactivation of production at some of the green schemes, in addition to the very good rains received in most crop-growing regions of our country, there is hope that the situation of those that were reported to be food insecure during the period would improve for the better.”

a5482.speaker: European Commission (press release)
a5482.name: European Commission (press release)
a5482.speech: Urges donors to improve aid effectiveness in order to achieve the Millennium Development Goals.

a5482.speaker: Louis Michel, Member of the European Commission responsible for development and humanitarian aid
a5482.name: Louis Michel
a5482.title: Member of the European Commission responsible for development and humanitarian aid
a5482.speech: "It is now or never. The Accra conference must sound the much-needed wake-up call for donors and developing countries. Since the Paris Declaration, it can be said that the easiest parts of the programme defined at that time have been implemented. The hardest part, however, is still to come. Today, the challenge consists in translating those words into deeds on a large scale."

a5482.speaker: European Union
a5482.name: European Union
a5482.speech: Within the framework of the international conference on aid effectiveness, the EU proposes focusing action on four areas: division of labour among donors; predictability of aid, with donors programming aid flows over at least three years; use of national systems, helping governments set their own priorities including by contributing financially to national budgets; and focusing on results to be defined by common agreement with partner countries instead of imposing a series of different conditions.

a5679.speaker: Demonstrators from the “No Azure for Apartheid” campaign (current and former Microsoft employees)
a5679.name: Demonstrators from the “No Azure for Apartheid” campaign (current and former Microsoft employees)
a5679.speech: Called, as part of a campaign called “No Azure for Apartheid”, for an end to cooperation with the Israeli government, amid accusations that Microsoft’s services are being used to support military operations against Palestinians in Gaza.

a5867.speaker: Gideon Enoch Abbequaye, Registrar and Secretary to the University of Cape Coast governing council (letter)
a5867.name: Gideon Enoch Abbequaye
a5867.title: Registrar and Secretary to the University of Cape Coast governing council (letter)
a5867.speech: A letter signed by the Registrar said Prof. Aheto as the Pro Vice-Chancellor was appointed at a special meeting on December 19, 2024.

a5949.speaker: African Union (declaration)
a5949.name: African Union (declaration)
a5949.speech: Declared 2024 the year of education for Africa.

a5970.speaker: Brigadier General Abdourahamane Tiani, President of the National Council for the Safeguard of the Homeland (CNSP) and Head of State of Niger
a5970.name: Brigadier General Abdourahamane Tiani
a5970.title: President of the National Council for the Safeguard of the Homeland (CNSP) and Head of State of Niger
a5970.speech: On the evening of 17 December 2024, on the eve of the 66th anniversary of the proclamation of the Republic, said what the CNSP and the government have in fact achieved, setting out urbi et orbi, to the country and to the world, what the sons and daughters of the Nation have together achieved over more than a year, and traced with drive and dexterity the new, hope-bearing trajectory on which the country has been set for more than a year.

a5970.speaker: Brigadier General Abdourahamane Tiani, President of the CNSP and Head of State of Niger
a5970.name: Brigadier General Abdourahamane Tiani
a5970.title: President of the CNSP and Head of State of Niger
a5970.speech: Advocated that all these successes, patent proof of the country's true independence, are to be capitalised upon and above all made to last, indeed to be set within a global and coherent vision in order to found a genuine political and social project.

a6065.speaker: Cargo experts (unnamed)
a6065.name: Cargo experts (unnamed)
a6065.speech: said that air freights to the U.S from Nigeria are informal and not in commercial quantity; the experts also differed on the impact of the tariff hike on the Nigerian economy, but agreed that Nigeria needed diplomacy to resolve the issue with the North American country ; cargo experts also fear that the new tariffs may compel some of the customs agents to close shop, while disengagement of workers may be on the increase, thereby having a negative effect on the Nigerian economy.

a6065.speaker: Otunba Frank Ogunojemite, President of the Africa Association of Professional Freight Forwarders and Logistics of Nigeria (APFFLON)
a6065.name: Otunba Frank Ogunojemite
a6065.title: President of the Africa Association of Professional Freight Forwarders and Logistics of Nigeria (APFFLON)
a6065.speech: said that the 14 percent tariff hike would have an adverse effect on Nigerian exports to the U.S.; according to him, it would increase the costs of exports, thereby making products from Nigeria less competitive relative to domestic and non-tariffed foreign goods; he emphasised that sectors heavily reliant on exports, such as agriculture and textiles, may suffer more than others, potentially leading to job losses and economic strain in Nigeria; Ogunojemite warned that Trump’s 14 percent tariff could have several significant effects on air freights from Nigeria, impacting costs, supply chains, trade relations, and economic conditions in both Nigeria and the U.S.; he regretted that the tariff imposition may disrupt already established supply chains, while manufacturers and suppliers who rely on Nigerian exports may have to seek alternative sources; he also expressed worries that the new tariff could be a barrier to trade, leading to tensions between the two countries and potentially affecting broader diplomatic relations. He added: “Businesses might require time to adjust their sourcing strategies, affecting overall trade volumes in the short term. Also, exporters may have to absorb some of these costs, which could reduce their profit margins or lead to increased prices for consumers. Some exporters might consider switching from air freight to ocean freight due to cost considerations. This could slow down the speed of shipments, but reduce costs. If air freight from Nigeria decreases due to higher tariffs, airlines may have to adjust their capacity and routes, which could impact the overall logistics network. Ultimately, U.S. consumers may feel the impact through higher prices for Nigerian goods, which could influence consumption patterns and affect overall demand.” He, however, advised that the government and cargo players, including logistics providers, should closely monitor the situation and adapt their strategies accordingly to mitigate adverse effects.

a6065.speaker: Amos Akpan, cargo analyst
a6065.name: Amos Akpan
a6065.title: cargo analyst
a6065.speech: said that almost all air freights from Nigeria to the US were private, unrecorded items, carried in the belly hold of passenger flights, insisting that the tariff imposition would have little or no effect on freights through the air from Nigeria; according to him, most of the exports lacked the Central Bank of Nigeria’s (CBN) Form M, while a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) between the Nigerian and the U.S agents was nonexistent. “No capture in recognised official documents. How do you apply tariffs on such transactions? We can only quote figures in tonnes/kilogrammes of what the airlines carried over a period, not as trade transactions between the two countries. Informal, undocumented trade carried out by private individuals forms the bulk of exports by air from Nigeria to the USA. If you are looking for formal trade transactions that we can place the discussions on tariff, go to sea freight where the following are shipped: oil and gas, agricultural produce and solid minerals.”

a6065.speaker: Dr. Segun Musa, Deputy National President of the National Association of Government Approved Freight Forwarders (NAGAFF)
a6065.name: Dr. Segun Musa
a6065.title: Deputy National President of the National Association of Government Approved Freight Forwarders (NAGAFF)
a6065.speech: said that the tariff sanction was coming on Nigeria’s exports at a time the country was making efforts to build and increase its trade in the America corridor; Musa, like Ogunojemite, declared that the sanction would have a minimal effect on exports, as Nigeria has limited volume going to America; he expressed that airfreight exports to America were mostly food commodities, which are in minimal commercial quantity, but necessary due to the Nigerian population living in America; he pointed out that with this sanction, trade between the two countries would be frosty, while customers from America would perceive Nigeria as a secondary market, rather than primary market; Musa regretted that the new tariff, when eventually implemented, would lead to exorbitant rates of Nigerian cargo, increase the existing gap of trade imbalance between the two countries and cut short air freight traffic to the U.S.; he further emphasised that the hike would have a toll on the increased trade projection from $3.42 billion in 2024 and $5.64 billion by 2029 from Nigeria to the U.S. He added: “Before now, we were looking at how to negotiate with these western countries, especially America and European countries on how we can improve and increase our taxes. If you observe recently, most of us in Africa, we have been clamouring on conventions that will ensure the western world reduce aids to us in Africa and in particularly Nigeria and give us the room under favourable business condition, but this tariff sanction will further affect that strategy and our traffic to the U.S will reduce drastically. When the trade traffic reduces, it’s also going to affect the freights – imports and exports. Presently, we don’t enjoy competitive air freights from Nigeria to America because we don’t have the volume. The higher the volume, the lower the rates. With this, the export freight rate is going to increase and this will also increase the import.” According to Musa, more of the foreign airlines would depart empty out of Nigeria with the implementation of the new tariff, thereby adding to import costs.

a6136.speaker: Royal Cabinet of Morocco (communique)
a6136.name: Royal Cabinet of Morocco (communique)
a6136.speech: Announced that “His Majesty King Mohammed VI, may God assist Him, held talks today at the Royal Palace in Rabat with the President of the French Republic, H.E. Mr Emmanuel Macron, who is making a State Visit to Morocco from 28 to 30 October at the invitation of the Sovereign”, and that the talks concerned the transition to a new era in relations between Morocco and France, within the framework of a renewed Exceptional Partnership and a strategic roadmap for the years to come.

a6136.speaker: King Mohammed VI of Morocco and Emmanuel Macron, President of France (joint position in the communique)
a6136.name: King Mohammed VI of Morocco and Emmanuel Macron
a6136.title: President of France (joint position in the communique)
a6136.speech: The two Heads of State intend, through this renewed partnership, to give a decisive impetus to the multidimensional relations of excellence between Morocco and France ; agreed to work together to strengthen the Euro-Mediterranean, African and Atlantic projection, in a common approach in favour of prosperity and human and sustainable development ; stressed the importance of renewing, in depth, the partnership between the two shores of the Mediterranean, in order to build a more stable, sustainable and prosperous future for the whole region, while responding to current socio-economic and environmental challenges.

a6136.speaker: Emmanuel Macron, President of France
a6136.name: Emmanuel Macron
a6136.title: President of France
a6136.speech: Hailed the constructive role of His Majesty King Mohammed VI, Chairman of the Al-Quds Committee, in the service of peace in the Middle East.

a6136.speaker: King Mohammed VI of Morocco and Emmanuel Macron, President of France (joint position in the communique)
a6136.name: King Mohammed VI of Morocco and Emmanuel Macron
a6136.title: President of France (joint position in the communique)
a6136.speech: Called for an immediate cessation of the attacks in Gaza and Lebanon, while stressing the priority of protecting civilian populations, and the importance of guaranteeing and facilitating the delivery of sufficient humanitarian aid, while putting an end to the regional conflagration ; recalled the urgency of reactivating the peace process, within the framework of the two-State solution, with an independent Palestinian State, on the borders of 4 June 1967, with East Jerusalem as its Capital.

a6136.speaker: Emmanuel Macron, President of France
a6136.name: Emmanuel Macron
a6136.title: President of France
a6136.speech: Extended an official invitation to His Majesty King Mohammed VI to make a State visit to France.

a6136.speaker: King Mohammed VI of Morocco
a6136.name: King Mohammed VI of Morocco
a6136.speech: Accepted the invitation, whose date will be agreed through diplomatic channels.

a6196.speaker: Minister of Livestock of Benin (communique)
a6196.name: Minister of Livestock of Benin (communique)
a6196.speech: Formally prohibits, until further notice, the importation, transit and distribution of poultry, parts and offal of frozen poultry, day-old chicks, eggs, animal feed and all other poultry-based preparations coming from Nigeria.

a6196.speaker: Byll Kperou Gado, Director of Livestock of Benin
a6196.name: Byll Kperou Gado
a6196.title: Director of Livestock of Benin
a6196.speech: In remarks delivered after the seizure, was reassuring with regard to the measures of the competent services to prevent the spread of the avian influenza virus on Beninese soil; urged the population to avoid any contact with poultry and to cook poultry-based food thoroughly; and advised farmers not to orient their poultry houses in the direction of the prevailing winds, given that wind is also a vector for the spread of the virus.

a6592.speaker: African National Congress (ANC) policy document / Resolutions of the ANC's 53rd National Conference
a6592.name: African National Congress (ANC) policy document / Resolutions of the ANC's 53rd National Conference
a6592.speech: The party's document states its precepts: "1. The ANC [is] in pursuit of its international relations objectives as directed by the Freedom Charter which states that 'there shall be peace and friendship'. Therefore, International Relations is utilised by the ANC to form friendships and to work towards peace in the continent and in the world, whilst pursuing South Africa's national interest; 2. The ANC's international relations policy is directly informed by our domestic policy, and vice versa, and they are mutually reinforcing; 3. The ANC remains committed to its founding values of a struggle for a humane, just, equitable, democratic, and free world; 4. The development and prosperity of Africa remains the central objective of the ANC's international perspective and policy for purposes of advancing the African Renaissance; and, 5. The ANC's international relations work is underpinned by a commitment to development, democracy, human rights, peace and security in the world."

a6592.speaker: African National Congress (ANC) policy document
a6592.name: African National Congress (ANC) policy document
a6592.speech: Speaks extensively to a "global contest between progressive and reactionary ideological perspectives on world affairs", devoting considerable space to the AU, the Pan African Parliament, the Pan-African Women's Organisation and the All-Africa Student Union, and speaking at length to conflicts involving Mali, Sudan/South Sudan, Swaziland, Guinea-Bissau, Iran, Cuba (the Cuban Guantanamo Five prisoners) and Syria, as well as hoped-for changes in the UN, IMF and World Bank and the theme "Continental and International Solidarity".

a6592.speaker: African National Congress (ANC) policy document
a6592.name: African National Congress (ANC) policy document
a6592.speech: On economic issues, the document says "Economic diplomacy reinforces our vision of a better Africa and better world as well as the achievement of national development objectives, believing that there can be no peace without development nor development without peace" and that "South Africa's economic diplomacy should serve as a tool of foreign policy including the utilisation of state-owned enterprises in development projects on the African continent."

a6592.speaker: African National Congress (ANC) policy document
a6592.name: African National Congress (ANC) policy document
a6592.speech: On its opposition to Africom, argues that "African states should be resolute in their stance against United State's Africom presence in Africa under the guise of 'War on Terror', while actually militarising the continent" and that "The ANC recognises that the Africom is more than just the building of American bases on the African continent, but it includes more subtle programmes involving the US and Nato military in military training of African militaries, the funding of NGOs for anti-African agendas and increasingly the introduction of drones under the guise of technological assistance in conflict areas."

a6592.speaker: African National Congress (ANC) policy document
a6592.name: African National Congress (ANC) policy document
a6592.speech: Notes the need for a "combined programme on international relations involving Alliance partners that needs to be developed that would include the issues of climate change, trade, foreign direct investment, industrialisation of Africa and transformation of multi-lateral institutions and global governance," as well as "Solidarity campaigns on Cuba, Western Sahara, Palestine and Swaziland, with a special discussion on our position on Swaziland" and affiliations with organisations like the "Socialist International, the Sao Paulo Forum, the Non-Aligned Movement and so forth".

a6592.speaker: South African Department of International Relations and Cooperation (Dirco) (Strategic Plan, 2010-2013)
a6592.name: South African Department of International Relations and Cooperation (Dirco) (Strategic Plan
a6592.speech: Prioritises key themes, saying in part: "[S]trengthening of relations with strategic formations of the North. Our approach will be to pursue a developmental and investment-orientated engagement that seeks to advance South Africa, the African continent and the rest of the South's development agenda… our relations with countries of the North have been and continue to be a source of increased investment, trade opportunities, as well as development cooperation for South Africa." ; "…to follow up on all commitments made by such multilateral groupings like the G8… we will continue to garner support from the developed countries of the North for South Africa's National Priorities, i.e. Health, Education, Land reform and Rural development, Creation of decent jobs, and our Fight against crime." ; "Our participation in the global system of governance is fundamentally premised on our commitment to work towards global political and socio-economic stability and security. The end of the first decade of the 21st century has witnessed the emergence of major powers of the South, with formidable alliances being formed and others revitalized…" ; "South Africa will continue to broaden and intensify its relations with BRIC member-countries, as they are key players in the current wave of globalisation – especially as it relates to the domain of technological innovation." ; "We seek to promote development, security, human rights and international law through our participation in the United Nations system and its specialised agencies. South Africa recognises the need to address the pressing social and economic challenges of developing countries, particularly those facing Africa. We still believe that the resolution of international conflicts should be peaceful and in accordance with the centrality of the UN Charter and the principles of international law…." ; "South Africa's international engagement on issues of climate change and energy security will continue to be guided by the principle of sustainable development. This principle seeks to ensure that we can enhance our economic growth without undue cost to the environment, while promoting social justice at the same time…" ; and, summing up its tasks in an uncertain world, "…Dirco should be seized with the question: how can we help push the frontiers of poverty and underdevelopment and ensure we extend the reach of our potential as a country?"

a6877.speaker: Dr David Pagwesese Parirenyatwa, President of the International Conference on AIDS and STIs in Africa (ICASA)
a6877.name: Dr David Pagwesese Parirenyatwa
a6877.title: President of the International Conference on AIDS and STIs in Africa (ICASA)
a6877.speech: called on African heads of state to honour the 15 per cent health budget commitment promised under the Abuja declaration; said the 2030 Millennium Development Goals were five years away and if they did not prioritise health and put it at the forefront of the Africa development agenda, they would not be able to meet the 95-95-95 HIV target ; “We are aware a few of the African countries have already reached that target, but the majority have not yet. There is no way we can make meaningful progress in the fight against HIV and AIDS and other diseases without significant increases in health funding and commitment from African governments.”

a6877.speaker: Dr David Pagwesese Parirenyatwa, President of the International Conference on AIDS and STIs in Africa (ICASA)
a6877.name: Dr David Pagwesese Parirenyatwa
a6877.title: President of the International Conference on AIDS and STIs in Africa (ICASA)
a6877.speech: said health was not a cost but rather an investment in economic and social development, adding that Africa must take its own resources like diamonds, gold and oil and invest them into the health systems of their respective countries ; quoting the World Bank's key demographic projections, said Africa's population would reach a record 1.7 billion by 2040, with 40 per cent being under the age of 15 years, and asked how the continent would ensure that future workforce was productive and able to contribute to the continent's development when the continent did not have at least a basic functional universal healthcare system ; “Let us not wait any longer. It is time we produce our own vaccines and medications. We hope that this will reduce our dependence on foreign aid and pharmaceutical imports.” ; stated that all Africans needed to know their HIV health status, saying this could not be ignored in this era where there had been scientific breakthroughs, including pre or post-exposure prophylaxis access, injectable treatment and all other tools that could be used maximally in every country.

a6877.speaker: World Bank key demographic projections
a6877.name: World Bank key demographic projections
a6877.speech: quoted as projecting that Africa's population would reach a record 1.7 billion by 2040, with 40 per cent being under the age of 15 years.

a6877.speaker: Dr Hafez Adam Taher, Director of Technical Coordination at the Ministry of Health, Ghana (speaking on behalf of the sector minister)
a6877.name: Dr Hafez Adam Taher
a6877.title: Director of Technical Coordination at the Ministry of Health, Ghana (speaking on behalf of the sector minister)
a6877.speech: said Ghana's hosting of ICASA 2025 came at a time when it had made notable strides in its national response to HIV-AIDS; mentioned these to include expansion of access to antiretroviral therapy, reduction of mother-to-child transmission and improving community-based care and support services.

a6877.speaker: Dr Kyeremeh Atuahene, Director General of the Ghana AIDS Commission
a6877.name: Dr Kyeremeh Atuahene
a6877.title: Director General of the Ghana AIDS Commission
a6877.speech: expressed the readiness of the commission to host the conference, elaborating that they were already setting up a national planning committee in conjunction with the organisers so that they would be driving all the activities in terms of planning, organisation and administration of the conference.

a7020.speaker: Vitali M. Boton, Head of the Communication Unit and Spokesperson of the President of the National Assembly of Benin
a7020.name: Vitali M. Boton
a7020.title: Head of the Communication Unit and Spokesperson of the President of the National Assembly of Benin
a7020.speech: Reviewed the record of the past session and the state of the partnership between the press and the parliamentary institution ; “I am particularly happy to be with you this evening on the occasion of our traditional press dinner, which has become, session after session, a convivial but essential forum for taking stock, holding dialogue and strengthening the bonds of trust between Parliament and the media”; “On behalf of the President of the National Assembly, Mr Louis Gbèhounou VLAVONOU, I would like to thank you for your massive attendance at this exchange.”

a7020.speaker: Vitali M. Boton, Spokesperson of the President of the National Assembly of Benin
a7020.name: Vitali M. Boton
a7020.title: Spokesperson of the President of the National Assembly of Benin
a7020.speech: Said the President of the National Assembly has always been convinced that a free, professional and informed press is an indispensable lever for democratic anchoring and for the standing of Parliament, which is why he insisted that this framework of exchanges be maintained and enriched.

a7020.speaker: Vitali M. Boton, Spokesperson of the President of the National Assembly of Benin
a7020.name: Vitali M. Boton
a7020.title: Spokesperson of the President of the National Assembly of Benin
a7020.speech: Reported on legislative output: the first ordinary session of 2025 opened on Thursday 10 April 2025; deputies of the ninth legislature met in ten plenary sittings and examined a total of 10 ordinary laws, 2 resolutions and 14 decrees ratifying loan agreements, covering fields from the Global Green Growth Institute accession, Beninese nationality for Afro-descendants, identification of natural persons, the Abidjan Convention protocols, microfinance regulation, entry and residence of foreigners, the national development vision to 2060, the Niger-Benin export pipeline, the organic law on the Constitutional Court, and associations and foundations; the Assembly also adopted at second reading law n° 2025-06 amending the code of criminal procedure.

a7020.speaker: Vitali M. Boton, Spokesperson of the President of the National Assembly of Benin
a7020.name: Vitali M. Boton
a7020.title: Spokesperson of the President of the National Assembly of Benin
a7020.speech: Said that during the past session no oral or written question to the government was examined in plenary, and that although this may seem to be a lack of parliamentary activity it is not, being explained by the stated wish to reinvigorate parliamentary oversight through more effective field missions anchored in local realities, and by the end-of-legislature context; said that under the impetus of President Louis Gbèhounou VLAVONOU Parliament favoured active oversight missions and that the Bureau of the National Assembly is working to strengthen the complementarity between field missions and questions in plenary in coming sessions.

a7020.speaker: Vitali M. Boton, Spokesperson of the President of the National Assembly of Benin
a7020.name: Vitali M. Boton
a7020.title: Spokesperson of the President of the National Assembly of Benin
a7020.speech: Cited other major activities of the session: the President’s activity report presented in plenary on Friday 25 April 2025 and adopted by a large majority; the Budget Orientation Debate for 2026-2028 held on Friday 27 June 2025; two international summits hosted in Benin (the World Summit on the Information Society in Africa in Cotonou, 14-16 May 2025, and the 31st Africa Regional Assembly of the Parliamentary Assembly of the Francophonie in Cotonou, 2-3 June 2025); and the strengthening of institutional partnerships, including the IPaB-NILDS memorandum of understanding workshop, the installation of the 4th Youth Parliament of Benin, and a cooperation and mutual assistance agreement signed with the Court of Auditors.

a7020.speaker: Vitali M. Boton, Spokesperson of the President of the National Assembly of Benin
a7020.name: Vitali M. Boton
a7020.title: Spokesperson of the President of the National Assembly of Benin
a7020.speech: On the partnership with the press: renewed the Assembly’s gratitude to press organs for their commitment and professionalism, saying that thanks to them parliamentary activities are relayed, explained, analysed and brought to the attention of national and international public opinion; noted with regret that certain press organs that collaborated with the institution had their legal existence called into question by decision n°25-033/HAAC of 22 May 2025, which did not allow the National Assembly to renew their service contracts for the current year; warmly congratulated the press organs officially recognised by the HAAC.

a7020.speaker: Louis Gbèhounou Vlavonou, President of the National Assembly of Benin (via his spokesperson)
a7020.name: Louis Gbèhounou Vlavonou
a7020.title: President of the National Assembly of Benin (via his spokesperson)
a7020.speech: Strongly urges the managers of the press organs concerned to complete the required formalities with the competent institutions, notably the High Authority for Audiovisual Media and Communication (HAAC), with a view to recovering their legality and once again being able to enjoy the confidence of Parliament.

a7020.speaker: Vitali M. Boton, Spokesperson of the President of the National Assembly of Benin
a7020.name: Vitali M. Boton
a7020.title: Spokesperson of the President of the National Assembly of Benin
a7020.speech: Concluded that the first ordinary session of 2025 ends on a note of intense satisfaction, remarkable in the quality of the texts adopted, the dynamism of parliamentary oversight and the vitality of cooperation and parliamentary diplomacy; said none of it would have been possible without the enlightened and methodical leadership of President Louis Gbèhounou VLAVONOU, who after nearly seven years at the head of Parliament embodies a new parliamentary culture of rigour, dialogue, responsibility and modernity, and to whom the Beninese people owe a more visible, more effective, closer and more respected National Assembly.

a7020.speaker: Constitution of Benin, article 145 paragraph 2 (cited)
a7020.name: Constitution of Benin
a7020.title: article 145 paragraph 2 (cited)
a7020.speech: “Financing agreements submitted for ratification are ratified by the President of the Republic, who reports on them to the National Assembly within a period of ninety days.”

a7020.speaker: High Authority for Audiovisual Media and Communication (HAAC) decision n°25-033/HAAC of 22 May 2025
a7020.name: High Authority for Audiovisual Media and Communication (HAAC) decision n°25-033/HAAC of 22 May 2025
a7020.speech: Established the official list of press organs recognised in Benin, calling into question the legal existence of certain press organs that had been collaborating with the National Assembly.

a7156.speaker: Sergeant Lamin Touray, Gambia Immigration Department officer
a7156.name: Sergeant Lamin Touray
a7156.title: Gambia Immigration Department officer
a7156.speech: “What you are talking about is sensitive. So, I can’t just respond to you on the telephone like that. I have to secure myself,” he said.

a7156.speaker: Sergeant Lamin Touray, Gambia Immigration Department officer
a7156.name: Sergeant Lamin Touray
a7156.title: Gambia Immigration Department officer
a7156.speech: Asked Fatima to pay D15,000 (approximately US$217), but they later agreed on a cost of D13,000 (approximately $183): “Let’s make it 13,000. Anyway, I cannot go beyond 13,000. I can produce it (passport) quickly. You are begging me that’s why I said I will make it 13,000, but if you don’t pay 13,000, I can’t make it,’ he said. ; Told Fatima that he had helped people in urgent need quickly get their passports after they paid him, saying ‘they paid me big money and they got it’. ; “You people are not serious. Do you think this is a small job?“ he asked.

a7156.speaker: Sergeant Lamin Touray, Gambia Immigration Department officer
a7156.name: Sergeant Lamin Touray
a7156.title: Gambia Immigration Department officer
a7156.speech: Requested the money be paid in full, in cash, as he does not accept instalments: ”You may not have time but if you can give it to me hand to hand it is better but a Wave also is possible. It is up to you,” he said. ; Asked Fatima to pay the money and then provide the pictures of the applicant, full name, and date of birth, plus the applicant’s mother’s national identity card: “If you give me all that information, then the rest is my work?” he said.

a7156.speaker: Sergeant Lamin Touray, Gambia Immigration Department officer
a7156.name: Sergeant Lamin Touray
a7156.title: Gambia Immigration Department officer
a7156.speech: “You know he is without any single document. So I am the one to provide that,” Touray told Fatima in one of their telephone conversations. ; “When he was here, was he able to speak Wolof or other local languages?’ the Sergeant asked about the applicant.

a7156.speaker: Malagen (investigative report)
a7156.name: Malagen (investigative report)
a7156.speech: Revealed that there are many ineligible individuals holding Gambian passports, including diplomatic and service passports, through bribery; also reported that non-nationals with illegally obtained documents may reside and rent properties, open bank accounts and may even be involved in money laundering.

a7156.speaker: 2022 National Audit Report
a7156.name: 2022 National Audit Report
a7156.speech: Found the Gambia Immigration Department (GID) at risk of exchanging passports for cash to ineligible people including non-Gambians: “We also noted that printed biometric and machine-readable passports in respect of 426 diplomatic and 71 service passports and their respective files maintained by GID did not reflect similar records maintained by MoFA,“ the Audit report stated. It also stated that there are 5,395 unaccounted passports produced by Gambian authorities, and that diplomatic passports were being used by certain individuals, but records of which couldn’t be traced in any official data.

a7156.speaker: The Republic (report)
a7156.name: The Republic (report)
a7156.speech: Revealed that the selling of national documents is not only limited to the passport but the birth certificate.

a7156.speaker: The Gambia Immigration Act 1996
a7156.name: The Gambia Immigration Act 1996
a7156.speech: Stated the requirements for a Gambian passport: any applicant should be screened to ensure there is no fraud on his or her part and should attend an interview when a first-time applicant; one needs to present a Gambian birth certificate or a Seyfor’s certificate, four passport-size photographs or National Identity Card, or a declaratory form completed and signed by a magistrate, a civil servant on grade 10 or above, Justice of the Peace or a notary public; and where there is doubt of the applicant’s nationality and neither parent is alive, an affidavit sworn by adult relatives.

a7156.speaker: The Constitution of The Gambia
a7156.name: The Constitution of The Gambia
a7156.speech: States how one could be a citizen of the Gambia by birth, descent, marriage or naturalisation — Section 9 (born in The Gambia with one Gambian parent), Subsection 10 (born outside The Gambia with one Gambian parent), Section 11 (married to a Gambian and resident 7 years), and Section 12 (naturalisation after about 15 years in The Gambia, of full age and capacity, good character and permanent residence).

a7156.speaker: Lamin S. Camara, Gambian legal expert
a7156.name: Lamin S. Camara
a7156.title: Gambian legal expert
a7156.speech: Said that when a document is ‘illegally’ provided to anyone, a crime has been committed by the issuing officers: “It could be abuse of office or official corruption by the issuing office.” ; Warned that if national documents, especially passports, are issued to non-Gambians and they abuse it, that poses profound consequences on the integrity of the nation and other holders too: ”States may not respect the privileges accorded to holders anymore. That will have an impact on national security too,’ he added. ; Added that selling of national documents would one day have a ‘profound effect’ on the political and socio-economic dynamics of The Gambia.

a7156.speaker: Muhammed Lenn, Adjunct Lecturer at the University of the Gambia
a7156.name: Muhammed Lenn
a7156.title: Adjunct Lecturer at the University of the Gambia
a7156.speech: “This can allow non-Gambians to sponsor political parties as well as vote during elections. While I don’t think we’ve reached that stage or likely to do so in the near future, the perception that national documents are being sold erodes public confidence in the electoral and security process/system,“ he said. ; Explained that selling national documents makes non-nationals compete with citizens to access services not meant or reserved for them, leading to unscrupulous people gaining access to public facilities, residing and renting properties, opening bank accounts and possibly money laundering.

a7156.speaker: The Guardian newspaper (story)
a7156.name: The Guardian newspaper (story)
a7156.speech: Revealed how former President Yahya Jammeh possessed three card-boxes of fake ID cards meant for paid foreigners to vote in the 2016 presidential election.

a7156.speaker: Spokesperson for the Gambia Immigration Department
a7156.name: Spokesperson for the Gambia Immigration Department
a7156.speech: Has been contacted for comments on this matter, but efforts to obtain his comments were not successful after several follow-ups by this reporter.

a7174.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
a7174.name: Donald Trump
a7174.title: US President
a7174.speech: Said he wants to turn a land like Palestine into a holiday resort, perhaps a private golf resort, and said he is donating the population of another country, 10,726 kilometres away, to other countries.

a7174.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
a7174.name: Donald Trump
a7174.title: US President
a7174.speech: Four years ago, as he was leaving office, issued an American Presidential Declaration donating an African country and member of the African Union, the Saharawi Arab Democratic Republic (SADR), better known as Western Sahara, to Morocco.

a7174.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
a7174.name: Donald Trump
a7174.title: US President
a7174.speech: This year, he says he has renamed the Gulf of Mexico as the Gulf of America — a name that has been in existence for over four centuries.

a7174.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
a7174.name: Donald Trump
a7174.title: US President
a7174.speech: Renamed the 100-year-old Panama Canal owned by Panama as the American Canal. In January, he threatened to seize the canal for allegedly making too much profit. Then a month later, he repeated his threat to invade and take over the canal, but this time for allegedly allowing the Chinese to run it.

a7174.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
a7174.name: Donald Trump
a7174.title: US President
a7174.speech: Threatened to seize Greenland from Denmark for America’s “economic security”.

a7174.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
a7174.name: Donald Trump
a7174.title: US President
a7174.speech: Asked neighbouring Canada to become the 51st state of the US and erase its 5,525-mile long border with it. He said of Canada: “If people wanted to play the game right, it would be 100 per cent certain that they’d become a state.”

a7174.speaker: Justin Trudeau, Canadian Prime Minister
a7174.name: Justin Trudeau
a7174.title: Canadian Prime Minister
a7174.speech: In February warned his country’s business leaders to take Trump’s threats seriously. He told them the Trump administration is “very aware of our resources, of what we have and they very much want to be able to benefit from those (Trump) has it in mind that one of the easiest ways of doing that is absorbing our country.” ; “Not only does the Trump administration know how many critical minerals we have, but that may be even why they keep talking about absorbing us and making us the 51st state.”

a7174.speaker: Trump administration
a7174.name: Trump administration
a7174.speech: Says it is targeting 600,000 immigrants whom it alleges have criminal records.

a7188.speaker: King Mohammed VI of Morocco (address to Parliament)
a7188.name: King Mohammed VI of Morocco (address to Parliament)
a7188.speech: Said that from the moment of his accession to the Throne he had affirmed Morocco's firm intention to move from mere management of the territorial-integrity question to a dynamic of change at home and abroad, and had called for abandoning a purely reactive approach in favour of initiative-taking, firmness and proactivity; that for years a determined and serene action had been conducted, despite a difficult international context, to demonstrate the soundness of Morocco's position and assert its legitimate historical rights over the Sahara, and that today “the Truth has been revealed with brilliance, for just Causes inevitably triumph.”

a7188.speaker: King Mohammed VI of Morocco (address to Parliament)
a7188.name: King Mohammed VI of Morocco (address to Parliament)
a7188.speech: Announced that the French Republic supports Morocco's sovereignty over the entire territory of the Sahara and backs the Autonomy Initiative within the framework of Moroccan territorial integrity as the sole basis for settling “this artificial regional conflict”, and expressed, in his own name and on behalf of the Moroccan people, “My warmest thanks and My deep gratitude to France and to His Excellency President Emmanuel Macron for this frank support for the Moroccan character of the Sahara”; noted that this position is carried by a permanent member of the Security Council with thorough knowledge of the conflict and reinforces UN efforts towards a political process leading to a definitive settlement under Moroccan sovereignty.

a7188.speaker: King Mohammed VI of Morocco (address to Parliament)
a7188.name: King Mohammed VI of Morocco (address to Parliament)
a7188.speech: Said Morocco had succeeded in obtaining recognition from influential countries that are permanent members of the Security Council, such as the United States of America and France; expressed pride in the positions of brotherly Arab and African countries supporting the Kingdom's territorial integrity, particularly those that have opened consulates in Laayoune and Dakhla; cited friendly Spain and most European Union countries as supporting the Autonomy Initiative; and thanked all countries that deal economically and through investment with the Kingdom's southern Provinces as an integral part of the national territory, placing the Moroccan Sahara at the heart of continental initiatives such as the Morocco-Nigeria gas pipeline project, the Process of the African Atlantic States and the initiative for Sahel countries' access to the Atlantic Ocean.

a7188.speaker: King Mohammed VI of Morocco (address to Parliament)
a7188.name: King Mohammed VI of Morocco (address to Parliament)
a7188.speech: Urged that the next stage requires greater mobilisation and vigilance to durably consolidate Morocco's position, that the fundamentals of Morocco's position must be explained to the small number of countries that continue to deny the logic of law and the facts of history, and that the efforts of all official, party and civil institutions must be pooled and better coordinated; called for greater coordination between the two chambers of Parliament through appropriate internal structures with qualified profiles and criteria of competence and specialisation in choosing delegations for bilateral meetings and regional and international forums, stressing the active role of party and parliamentary diplomacy.

a7188.speaker: King Mohammed VI of Morocco (address to Parliament)
a7188.name: King Mohammed VI of Morocco (address to Parliament)
a7188.speech: Saluted the efforts of national diplomacy, the institutions concerned, the vital forces of the Nation and all patriotic Moroccans at home and abroad in defending the Homeland's legitimate interests and thwarting the machinations of the enemies; thanked “our sons of the Sahara” for their unwavering loyalty and sacrifices; and reaffirmed in conclusion that Morocco will remain constantly firm in its position and faithful to the spirit of openness towards its Maghreb and regional environment, contributing to the common development, security and stability of the peoples of the region.

a7211.speaker: Daniel Chapo, Mozambican President
a7211.name: Daniel Chapo
a7211.title: Mozambican President
a7211.speech: Urged that the gospel of violence and hatred must be replaced by messages of love for one’s neighbour, at a rally on Friday in the northern city of Nampula. He repeatedly urged national unity, peace and forgiveness so that stability may rule in Mozambique ; “All religions preach love”, said Chapo. “We shall work closely with the people for the consolidation of peace and reconciliation. We shall do everything to stabilise the country and end violent demonstrations” ; “Politicians should preach love, forgiveness and reconciliation among Mozambique. Only thus will we achieve peace”, he said.

a7211.speaker: Daniel Chapo, Mozambican President
a7211.name: Daniel Chapo
a7211.title: Mozambican President
a7211.speech: Explained to the crowd the essence of the political undertaking he had signed in Maputo with nine political parties on 5 March. “The signing of this undertaking is not the end”, he said. “On the contrary, it’s the beginning and everyone should participate in it. The media, business people, academics, we must all sit down to discuss what has been going on with us over the past 30 years. For whenever elections are held, there are always problems. Let’s debate the deep causes of this problem”.

a7211.speaker: Daniel Chapo, Mozambican President
a7211.name: Daniel Chapo
a7211.title: Mozambican President
a7211.speech: Stressed that differences of opinion cannot justify violence. “Thinking differently is good”, he said, “but it cannot lead us to violence that generates violence, hatred that generates hatred. The law of life is that we reap what we sow, and so all Mozambicans should plant love”.

a7211.speaker: Daniel Chapo, Mozambican President
a7211.name: Daniel Chapo
a7211.title: Mozambican President
a7211.speech: Stressed the need for Mozambique to gain economic independence, so that the country no longer depends on foreign aid. “Independence will only be complete when we do not need to depend on others”, he said. “That’s why we say let’ work, let’s produce in industry, and even for export”.

a7211.speaker: Daniel Chapo, Mozambican President
a7211.name: Daniel Chapo
a7211.title: Mozambican President
a7211.speech: Evoked the 50th anniversary of Mozambican independence, which is celebrated this year, stressed that “the festivities of the 50 years should take place in an environment of peace and harmony and never in division”.

a7216.speaker: Hassan Sheikh Mohamud, President of the Federal Republic of Somalia
a7216.name: Hassan Sheikh Mohamud
a7216.title: President of the Federal Republic of Somalia
a7216.speech: Has expressed his strong support for the recent Gaza ceasefire agreement. The President lauded the dedicated efforts of Qatar, Egypt, and the United States in brokering this crucial agreement.

a7216.speaker: Hassan Sheikh Mohamud, President of the Federal Republic of Somalia
a7216.name: Hassan Sheikh Mohamud
a7216.title: President of the Federal Republic of Somalia
a7216.speech: Emphasized the need for sustained international and regional cooperation to reinforce the ceasefire and expedite the delivery of urgent humanitarian assistance to the people of Gaza. He highlighted the dire humanitarian situation in Gaza and called for immediate action to alleviate the suffering of its residents.

a7216.speaker: Hassan Sheikh Mohamud, President of the Federal Republic of Somalia
a7216.name: Hassan Sheikh Mohamud
a7216.title: President of the Federal Republic of Somalia
a7216.speech: Reiterated Somalia’s commitment to peace and justice, advocating for a just and lasting solution to establish an independent Palestinian state in accordance with the principle of two states. He urged the global community to seize this opportunity to promote peace and stability in the region.
